Pour notre site de production biotech et siège social de Meyrin, nous recherchons un Spécialiste Assurance Qualité (h/f).

Sous la supervision de la Responsable d’équipe Assurance Qualité, vous rejoignez une équipe de 5 personnes et votre mission consiste à garantir la qualité des produits fabriqués et le maintien de la conformité du site aux exigences BPF/GMP, tout en participant activement à l’amélioration continue.

 
Vos responsabilités principales sont les suivantes :Pour mener à bien cette mission, nous recherchons une personne ayant le profil suivant :

Réviser et approuver les dossiers de lots, protocoles de fabrication, rapports de qualification / validation, programmes de maintenance / étalonnage et autres documents qualité associés

Préparer les protocoles de libération

Assurer un support qualité dans la gestion des événements qualité (déviations, investigations, CAPA et demandes de changement) et contribuer à leur résolution

Veiller au respect des exigences réglementaires et la conformité des procédés conformément aux BPF, aux AMM et aux SOP et aux dossiers de validation

Contribuer à la préparation et au déroulement des audits, inspections et visites réglementaires

Participer à l'amélioration continue des systèmes qualité et de la documentation du site

Développer une présence terrain active afin de promouvoir la culture qualité et accompagner les équipes opérationnelles

Participer aux projets qualité transverses, au suivi des indicateurs de performance et à la formation des collaborateurs sur les bonnes pratiques GxP

Pour mener à bien cette mission, nous recherchons une personne ayant le profil suivant :

Formation supérieure en Pharmacie, Biologie, Biochimie, Chimie ou domaine équivalent

Au minimum 2 à 3 ans d'expérience dans l'industrie pharmaceutique ou biotechnologique dans un rôle lié à la qualité ou la production ; bonnes connaissances de processus de fabrication un réel atout

Solides connaissances des BPF, avec une bonne compréhension des systèmes qualité pharmaceutiques

Maîtrise de la Suite Ms Office et des systèmes ERP (idéalement Sage X3) ; expérience avec les outils Trackwise / EDMS / LMS valorisée

Excellente maîtrise du français, à l’oral comme à l’écrit ; anglais apprécié

Vous vous décrivez comme une personne rigoureuse, proactive et orientée solutions. Véritable team player, vous appréciez le travail au sein d’une équipe soudée et savez conjuguer assertivité et esprit de collaboration. Vous êtes capable de défendre avec conviction les exigences Qualité, tout en privilégiant le dialogue, le pragmatisme et la recherche de consensus. Grâce à votre esprit d’analyse, votre sens des responsabilités et votre excellent relationnel, vous interagissez efficacement avec différents départements et contribuez activement à promouvoir une culture qualité et collaborative forte.
 
Cette opportunité vous intéresse ? Transmettez-nous au plus vite votre candidature et rejoignez les équipes d'OM Pharma !

 

 
About Us

OM Pharma is a global Geneva-based biopharmaceutical company. It is a leader in the prevention of recurrent respiratory and urinary tract infections and is also active in the treatment of vascular diseases.

It operates worldwide through a strong network of international partners and invests its profits in R&D to develop microbial derived immunotherapeutic products to treat acute and chronic immunological disorders resulting from inflammation and infections. 

The company strives to improve the quality of life of patients around the world by providing access to better treatment of immunological imbalances.

For more information, visit the website: ompharma.com.

As a Mechanical Engineer for Vacuum you will join the team working on the vacuum systems for a future accelerator at CERN (FCC-ee) and contribute to the selection, characterisation and validation of materials and processes for ultra-high vacuum components. In this role, you will be involved in defining samples and prototypes, their production and procurement, as well as their testing and validation.
Your responsibilities
Actively participate in the development of the FCC-ee vacuum systems, particularly in materials and process selection, characterisation and validation, as well as prototyping.
Contribute to the internalisation and in-house development of key manufacturing technologies for large component production.
Collaborate with a dynamic team dedicated to the FCC-ee study.
Communicate regularly with CERN-wide services and external companies or institutes.
 
Your profile
Experience with metallic, in particular copper alloys, and ceramic materials for UHV applications.
Experience with metallic and ceramic additive manufacturing processes, including plasma spray, cold gas dynamic spray and 3D SLM printing.
Experience with metals hot and cold work processing and welding technologies. Experience with Laser and/or Friction Stir Welding is an advantage.
Skills
Fabrication of mechanical parts with CNC machine, in particular with CAM software.
Production of samples for materials characterisation including microscopic observations.
Prior knowledge or use of WorkNC is an advantage.
Design of mechanical parts with CAD program. Use of CATIA is an advantage.
Spoken and written English or French, with a commitment to learn the other language.
Eligibility criteria:
You are a national of a CERN Member or Associate Member State.
You have a professional background in Mechanical/Materials & Process Engineering (or a related field) and have either:
a Master's degree with 2 to 6 years of post-graduation professional experience;
or a PhD with no more than 3 years of post-graduation professional experience.
You have never had a CERN fellow or graduate contract before.

Join CERN's Polymer Laboratory within the Superconducting Magnet Technology section and contribute to the development and qualification of advanced polymer and composite materials.
In this role, you will take part in the design, validation and implementation of innovative materials for high-field superconducting magnets.
Your responsibilities:
Contribute to the development of novel polymer and composite materials for superconducting magnets, with particular emphasis on cryogenic operation, high-voltage insulation and radiation resistance.
Design and validate manufacturing and processing techniques for superconducting magnet insulation systems.
Contribute to the laboratory developments by identifying material technologies and processing techniques, as well as establishing new experimental capabilities.
Your profile:
Experience in material characterisation techniques, such as mechanical, thermal or chemical analyses.
Experience in composite and/or polymer processing techniques.
Knowledge of superconducting magnet construction and technologies, or of materials for cryogenic, high-voltage or radiation environments, would be an asset.
Skills:
Knowledge of materials science.
Knowledge and application of material testing.
Ability to work effectively within multidisciplinary teams.
Knowledge of cryogenics technology is a plus.
Spoken and written English, with a commitment to learn French.
Eligibility criteria:
You are a national of a CERN Member or Associate Member State.
You have a professional background in Material, Chemical, Mechanical Engineering (or a related field) and have either:
a Master's degree with 2 to 6 years of post-graduation professional experience;
or a PhD with no more than 3 years of post-graduation professional experience.
You have never had a CERN fellow or graduate contract before.

Au sein de l'unité de soins intensifs pédiatriques, vous accompagnez les enfants hospitalisés et leurs proches, à travers des médiations artistiques adaptées à leur état clinique et à leurs besoins spécifiques.
En collaboration avec l'équipe interdisciplinaire, vous contribuez à la prise en charge globale de l'enfant, notamment dans la gestion de l'anxiété et de la douleur, l'expression émotionnelle, la prévention du traumatisme médical, ainsi qu’à l'accompagnement des situations de fin de vie.
Les prises en charge individuelles se déroulent au lit du ou de la patiente ou en chambre d'isolement, nécessitant une adaptation constante aux contraintes de l'environnement de soins intensifs (hygiène, asepsie et prévention des infections).
À partir de votre évaluation clinique, vous identifiez les besoins de l'enfant et de sa famille, définissez des objectifs thérapeutiques individualisés et assurez la traçabilité des interventions dans le dossier patient.
Grâce à des moyens variées tels que le dessin, le modelage, le conte, la musique, les marionnettes ou le collage, vous favorisez l'expression émotionnelle, le développement des ressources de l'enfant et le soutien de son vécu d'hospitalisation.
Vous accompagnez les patients et patientes, du nourrisson à l'adolescent, confrontés à l'anxiété, à la douleur, aux soins invasifs ou aux conséquences du traumatisme médical, y compris lorsque les capacités de communication sont limitées ou absentes.
Avec les parents et les fratries, vous leur faites bénéficier d'un accompagnement adapté tout au long du parcours de soins, notamment dans les contextes de soins palliatifs, de fin de vie ou de deuil.
Dans le cadre des colloques interdisciplinaires et des transmissions cliniques, vous partagez vos observations et contribuez à l'élaboration de réponses thérapeutiques coordonnées.
Vous participez au développement des projets du service en lien avec le bien-être de l'enfant hospitalisé, les soins de développement et les soins palliatifs pédiatriques.
La gestion du matériel et le suivi du budget alloué à l'activité font également partie de vos responsabilités.
Auprès des équipes soignantes, vous valorisez l'apport de l'art-thérapie, partagez votre expertise et contribuez au développement de cette pratique au sein de l'institution.
Vous participez aux démarches d'évaluation et aux projets de recherche visant à enrichir les connaissances et les pratiques en art-thérapie hospitalière.

En tant que cheffe ou chef de clinique titulaire d’un titre de spécialiste en pneumologie, vous assurez l’ensemble des activités cliniques du service et évoluez dans un environnement universitaire, à l’interface des soins, de l’enseignement et de la recherche. Grâce à un tournus trimestriel au sein des différentes unités spécialisées, vous développez une expertise diversifiée couvrant aussi bien la pratique hospitalière qu’ambulatoire en faisant preuve de polyvalence. Vous intervenez notamment dans la prise en charge des pneumopathies interstitielles, des complications pulmonaires chez les patientes ou patients immunodéprimés, de la transplantation pulmonaire, de la pneumologie interventionnelle ainsi que des troubles respiratoires du sommeil, en collaboration étroite avec le Centre de médecine du sommeil.
Vous rejoignez une équipe soudée composée de 9 chefs et cheffes de clinique, 4 médecins adjoints et adjointes et 5 médecins internes, sous la responsabilité de la professeure cheffe de service. Vous collaborez étroitement avec une équipe pluridisciplinaire regroupant infirmiers et infirmières spécialisées, techniciens et techniciennes en physiologie respiratoire, personnel administratif ainsi que les différents centres et départements médicaux de l’institution.
Vous assurez la prise en charge diagnostique et thérapeutique des pathologies respiratoires aiguës et chroniques. Vous participez à l’évaluation et au suivi de situations complexes, incluant notamment la dyspnée, la tuberculose, l’insuffisance respiratoire et les différents domaines médico-techniques de la spécialité.
Vous faites preuve de résilience, de sens clinique et d’une grande capacité d’analyse dans la prise en charge de situations parfois complexes. Grâce à votre sens de l’organisation et à votre capacité à prioriser, vous assurez efficacement vos activités cliniques tout en répondant aux multiples sollicitations (patients et patientes, téléphones, correspondances, réunions). Vous veillez à maintenir une communication claire, bienveillante et adaptée avec les patients et patientes, leurs proches ainsi qu’avec l’ensemble des professionnels impliqués dans leur prise en charge, en adaptant votre discours à leur compréhension.
En vous appuyant sur votre esprit d’équipe, vous faites preuve de solidarité face aux imprévus. En tant que cheffe ou chef de clinique, vous participez activement à la supervision et à la formation des médecins internes du département de médecine dans le domaine de la pneumologie, en adoptant une posture de mentorat et en partageant votre expertise.

Vous participez, avec les préparatrices et préparateurs en pharmacie, les logisticiens et logisticiennes et les assistantes et assistants en pharmacie, à l’activité de pharmacien ou pharmacienne de routine de l’Unité de logistique pharmaceutique de la pharmacie des HUG. Vous assurez, sous la supervision des pharmaciennes et pharmaciens chefs de projets et adjoints ou adjointes, au bon fonctionnement de l’approvisionnement en médicaments et leur mise à disposition auprès des patients.
En collaboration avec deux autres pharmaciens et pharmaciennes, vous êtes le ou la référente pour les demandes diverses des médecins et unités de soins en lien avec l’obtention des médicaments, vous supervisez la gestion des ruptures, vous gérez les stocks de stupéfiants illicites. Vous assurez le suivi des prescriptions des médicaments critiques. Vous pilotez le processus de contrôle et retrait de lots avec le responsable assurance qualité.
Vous garantissez la mise en application de la politique du médicament et des procédures de qualité et de sécurité. Vous contribuez à l’amélioration continue de l’organisation, en collaboration étroite avec les autres pharmaciens et pharmaciennes de l’unité, y compris en participant aux séances transversales avec d’autres unités ou services (pharmacie clinique, production).
Vous participez à la formation et l’encadrement de collaboratrices et collaborateurs de la Pharmacie y compris apprenants et apprenantes (MAS, stagiaires).

Au sein du Service maintenance et optimisation des infrastructures (SMOI), vous prenez la responsabilité du secteur Electricité dont les installations sont critiques pour la sécurité de notre patientèle et le fonctionnement de l’institution.
À ce titre, vous pilotez l’ensemble des activités de maintenance, d’exploitation et de développement de ces installations techniques à haute sensibilité.
Vous définissez les objectifs opérationnels de votre secteur en cohérence avec la stratégie du service et en assurez le déploiement auprès de votre équipe.
Vous gérez une équipe de techniciennes et techniciens en les responsabilisant et en leur apportant le soutien et l’encadrement nécessaires au bon fonctionnement du secteur. Vous formez et donnez un support aux collaborateurs et collaboratrices exploitant les installations électriques.
Vous assurez la gestion des activités et des ressources humaines, matérielles et financières, en garantissant le respect des normes, des délais et des budgets.
Vous veillez à la conformité réglementaire des installations sous votre responsabilité, et garantissez un haut niveau de sécurité et de fiabilité des équipements.
Vous mettez en place et suivez des indicateurs de performance permettant de piloter l’efficacité de la maintenance préventive et curative, afin d’optimiser continuellement les pratiques de votre secteur.
Vous conduisez des projets techniques (mise en conformité, renouvellement d’installations, amélioration continue), en collaboration avec les services internes et partenaires externes.
Vous assurez une veille technologique et réglementaire afin d’anticiper les évolutions nécessaires des installations en lien avec les exigences médicales et les standards de sécurité.
Manager d’équipes spécialisées, vous veillez au développement des compétences, à la transmission du savoir-faire et à l’engagement de vos collaborateurs et collaboratrices. Vous favorisez une culture d’exigence, de collaboration et d’amélioration continue.
En tant que responsable technique, vous êtes titulaire de l’autorisation générale d’installer au sens de l’article 9 de l’OIBT. Vous êtes également l’ « Exploitant d’installation » au sens de l’OICF et de la directive ESTI 100.
Vous êtes également un interlocuteur ou une interlocutrice clé des utilisateurs et utilisatrices, en les conseillant sur les solutions techniques adaptées et en priorisant les interventions en fonction des enjeux de sécurité et de continuité des soins.

Dans le cadre de vos fonctions vous réalisez des évaluations neuropsychologiques d’adultes suivis au sein des différentes structures de soins de la psychiatrie adulte, des centres ambulatoires de psychiatrie ainsi qu’au sein de la consultation campus biotech Neurosciences cliniques.
Votre activité s’articule autour de patientes et patients présentant des psychopathologies variées (schizophrénie, tda-h, …) pouvant affecter la cognition, la motivation et la régulation émotionnelle.  Le travail comprend notamment l'utilisation de tests psychométriques structurés et standardisés (par ex. BACS, MATRIX MCCB) pertinents pour l'enquête standardisée dans un contexte clinique comme scientifique. Un travail de réhabilitation cognitive est également à développer.
Vous êtes amené ou amenée à collaborer avec différentes équipes :
Équipes multidisciplinaires de soin ambulatoire du service de psychiatrie adule (transmission des résultats et des conclusions de l’évaluation neuropsychologique)

Travail de liaison avec les psychologues travaillant dans les différentes structures ambulatoires du service

Collaboration avec les intervenants et intervenantes (équipes soignantes, chercheurs, …) de la consultation campus biotech neurosciences cliniques - psychiatrie

Vous participez également de manière active aux activités de recherche du service de psychiatrie adulte.
Plus globalement, vous évoluez dans un environnement qui valorise la collaboration, l’expertise clinique et le partage des connaissances, au service d’une prise en charge exigeante et humaine.

Job Description SummaryRole Type: Onsite working, #LI-Onsite
Location: Basel, Switzerland
Relocation Support: This role is based in Basel, Switzerland. Novartis is unable to offer relocation support: please only apply if accessible.

What if your expertise in in vivo oncology could help advance the next generation of radioligand therapies (RLT)? As a Research Scientist in our preclinical Radioligand Therapy team, you will develop and characterize oncology models, evaluate novel treatments, and generate insights that support our world-leading Oncology portfolio. Working collaboratively across global laboratory and project teams, you will apply your experience with rodents, pharmacology, bioanalysis, and imaging to help translate innovative science into potential new therapies for patients.

 
Job Description
Key Responsibilities 
Develop and characterize novel in vivo oncology models to support preclinical radioligand therapy research. 
Conduct efficacy studies evaluating novel radioligand therapies across oncology programs. 
Perform biodistribution studies and metabolite analyses to inform pharmacology decisions. 
Conduct small-animal positron emission tomography (PET), single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT), and computed tomography (CT) imaging studies.  
Support in vitro and ex vivo activities, including cell culture, flow cytometry, immunohistochemistry, immunofluorescence, autoradiography, polymerase chain reaction, and Western blotting.
 
Essential Requirements 
Bachelor's or Master's degree in Cell Biology, Medical Physics, Bioengineering, Biotechnology, Pharmacology, or a related field. 
Hands-on experience with rodent handling and in vivo oncology models, including dosing, sampling, and animal welfare requirements. 
Practical in vivo experience gained within an academic or industry biomedical research laboratory. 
Training and practical experience working safely with open radioactive sources. 
Advanced written and spoken English, with the ability to communicate scientific findings effectively. 

Desirable Requirements 
Experience with positron emission tomography, single-photon emission computed tomography, or computed tomography imaging in rodents and subsequent image analysis. 
Experience with cellular and molecular biology methods. 
Experience with immunohistochemistry, tissue processing, and sectioning. 
Strong collaboration, organization, and communication skills, with experience working across interdisciplinary and cross-site teams. (e.g. cell culture, flow cytometry, immunohistochemistry, immunofluorescence, autoradiography, PCR, Western blotting) 
 
Benefits & Rewards 
At Novartis, we’re committed to reimagining medicine together - and rewarding the people who make it happen. 

Expected Annual Base Salary Range for role: 

76,300.00 - 141,700.00 CHF Annual

The base salary offered is determined based on gender-neutral objectives, such as relevant skills, competencies and experience in accordance with the Novartis pay setting policy and upon joining Novartis will be reviewed periodically.

In addition to your base salary, you may be eligible for a performance-based bonus depending on certain performance parameters. 

The rewards of being part of our team go far beyond base pay and incentives. We also offer a variety of competitive benefits in kind to help you thrive personally and professionally, such as insurance plans, retirement plans, wellbeing resources and global recognition programs. In addition, we provide flexible and hybrid working options, where possible, and minimum 14 weeks paid parental leave.
   
In addition to your base salary, you may be eligible for a performance-based bonus depending on certain performance parameters. Long-term equity awards granted at group level may also be part of your package. Further details will be provided during the application process.  

Pay equity is a fundamental principle of our employment policy and reflects our commitment to create a diverse, equitable and inclusive environment that treats all employees with dignity and respect, as outlined in our Code of Ethics.   

Read our brochure to learn more about our global total rewards offering: 
https://www.novartis.com/sites/novartis_com/files/novartis-life-handbook.pdf 
  
Note: Benefits and compensation may vary by country and are subject to local legal requirements, including provisions of collective bargaining agreements where applicable. A full overview of your compensation package, including any relevant collective bargaining agreement details applicable to your role based on your employment location and Novartis employer entity, will be communicated separately to you during the application process. 

Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion / EEO
Novartis is committed to building an outstanding, inclusive work environment and diverse teams’ representative of the patients and communities we serve.

Accessibility and accommodation
Novartis is committed to working with and providing reasonable accommodation to all individuals. If, because of a medical condition or disability, you need a reasonable accommodation for any part of the recruitment process, or in order to receive more detailed information about the essential functions of a position, please send an e-mail to diversity.inclusion_ch@novartis.com and let us know the nature of your request and your contact information. Please include the job requisition number in your message.

Why Novartis
Helping people with disease and their families takes more than innovative science. It takes a community of smart, passionate people like you. Collaborating, supporting and inspiring each other. Combining to achieve breakthroughs that change patients’ lives. Ready to create a brighter future together? https://www.novartis.com/about/strategy/people-and-culture

What you'll do
You’ll take your first steps into the world of work at CERN — a place where learning and discovery go hand in hand. You’ll join a team of experts and contribute to real projects that connect science, technology and innovation. Every day will bring opportunities to learn new skills, explore your interests and see how your studies come to life.
Your responsibilities
Support experienced professionals in their daily activities.
Learn and apply new tools or methods relevant to your area of study.
Contribute to small-scale projects under the guidance of your supervisor.
Collaborate with people from diverse backgrounds and share ideas in an international environment.
Your profile
You are currently studying in a physics field.
You are required or encouraged by your university to complete a practical training period.
You are eager to develop your skills through on-the-job learning.
You enjoy teamwork and learning from others in a collaborative setting.
Your skills
Fundamental knowledge in your field of study.
Curiosity, precision and a proactive attitude towards learning.
Good communication skills and ability to work effectively in a multicultural team.

As a motivated young mechanical design engineer, with a specific interest in seeking practical solutions around mechanical systems, CERN's graduate program may very well give you that challenging opportunity.

The mandate of the MME group, within the Engineering Department (EN), is to provide to the CERN community specific engineering solutions combining mechanical design, fabrication and material sciences. Historically the group maintains and develops the know-how on the mechanical construction of beam accelerator components and physics detectors. You will join the Design Office that is in charge of mechanical design of components required for CERN's accelerator and detectors, comprising many high-tech equipment such as superconducting magnets and cavities, vacuum systems and instrumentation. And under the supervision of a senior design engineer, you will design and develop mechanical components and systems from concept to production.
What we offer:
A collaborative and innovative work environment.
Opportunities for professional growth and development.
Access to the latest tools and technologies.
Supportive team culture focused on achieving excellence.
Your responsibilities
Design and develop mechanical components and systems from concept to production.
Create detailed 3D models and 2D drawings using CATIA V5, adhering to ISO GPS norms.
Carry out simple structural analysis and numerical calculations.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams within the group, material science, manufacturing, and quality assurance, to ensure design feasibility and manufacturability.
Continuously improve designs based on feedback and testing results.
Participate in problem-solving and troubleshooting activities related to design and production issues.
Maintain accurate documentation of designs, modifications, and project progress.
Your profile
Initial experience in mechanical design and development of mechanical components or assemblies.
Knowledge of 3D CAD modelling and 2D technical drafting, preferably using CATIA V5
Understanding of mechanical engineering principles, including materials, manufacturing processes and mechanical behaviour of structures.
Skills
Proficiency in CAD software such as CATIA V5 for creating 3D & 2D drawings.
Strong understanding of ISO GPS norms and their application in mechanical design.
Practical knowledge of mechanics and mechanical systems.
Ability to learn new languages (French / English).
Spoken and written English, with a commitment to learn French.
Eligibility criteria:
You are a national of a CERN Member or Associate Member State.
By the application deadline, you have a maximum of two years of professional experience since graduation in Mechanical Engineering (or a related field) and your highest educational qualification is either a Bachelor's or Master's degree.
You have never had a CERN fellow or graduate contract before.
Applicants without University degree are not eligible.
Applicants with a PhD are not eligible.

Be part of the future of mobility at CERN and lead projects contributing to the delivery and evolution of CERN's mobility strategy. You will coordinate the implementation of the mobility plan, prepare the next mobility plan, and lead cross-functional projects and events that improve mobility across CERN sites.
Your responsibilities:
Coordinate and monitor the actions of CERN's mobility plan through to the 2028 horizon, including milestones, dependencies, risks, decisions and follow-up actions.
Maintain a consolidated project portfolio and ensure regular, reliable reporting on status, priorities, issues and forthcoming decisions.
Work with action owners and stakeholders to translate strategic objectives into practical workplans, deliverables and implementation steps.
Contribute to the preparation of the future CERN mobility plan by gathering needs, analysing lessons learned, structuring consultations and drafting supporting material.
Pilot mobility-related projects and events, from initial scoping and stakeholder alignment through implementation, operational coordination and post-event review.
Participate actively in the CERN mobility working group, prepare inputs and meetings, document conclusions, and coordinate agreed follow-up.
Support communication and stakeholder engagement on mobility initiatives, ensuring that information is clear, timely and adapted to the target audience.
Identify opportunities for service improvement, sustainability and better user experience, and formulate evidence-based recommendations for decision-making.
Ensure that project documentation, decisions, indicators and lessons learned are recorded and accessible for continuity and governance purposes.
Your profile:
Graduated in Project Management, Transport and Mobility, Urban Planning, Sustainability, Engineering, Business Administration, Public Policy or a related field.
Initial experience in project coordination, multi-stakeholder initiatives, mobility, events, sustainability or service development would be an asset.
Experience in an international or multidisciplinary environment would be an advantage.
Skills:
Ability to structure and monitor projects, action plans, milestones, risks and deliverables.
Strong analytical and drafting skills, with the ability to turn varied inputs into concise reports and recommendations.
Good command of common office, collaboration, presentation and project-tracking tools.
Ability to organise meetings, workshops and events and to ensure systematic follow-up.
Interest in sustainable mobility, transport services and user-centred service improvement.
Clear communication and stakeholder management.
Ability to work autonomously while escalating risks and decisions appropriately.
Spoken and written English or French, with a commitment to learn the other language.
Eligibility criteria:
You are a national of a CERN Member or Associate Member State.
You have a professional background in Transportation Management, Civil Engineering (or a related field) and have either:
a Master's degree with 2 to 6 years of post-graduation professional experience;
or a PhD with no more than 3 years of post-graduation professional experience.
You have never had a CERN fellow or graduate contract before.

À la Clinique de Crans-Montana, l’équipe de cuisine prépare chaque jour environ 180 repas destinés aux patientes et patients ainsi qu’au personnel de l’institution. Elle propose également une offre de petite restauration à la cafétéria. Sa mission est de garantir une alimentation équilibrée, variée et savoureuse, répondant aux recommandations nutritionnelles suisses et élaborée dans le respect des normes d’hygiène et de sécurité alimentaire. Labellisé « Cuisinons notre région » et « Fourchette verte », le service privilégie les produits frais et locaux afin de valoriser les saveurs du terroir.
En tant qu’apprenti ou apprentie cuisinière, vous participez à la préparation et à la réalisation de plats destinés à une clientèle variée, tout en tenant compte des régimes alimentaires spécifiques liés au milieu hospitalier.
La diversité des prestations et les exigences propres à notre environnement de soins vous permettent de bénéficier d’une formation riche et complète. Vous découvrez l’ensemble des postes de la cuisine et développez progressivement vos compétences techniques et organisationnelles.
Au cours de votre formation, vous apprenez les techniques de préparation et de cuisson des aliments, les règles d’hygiène et de sécurité alimentaire, ainsi que les bases de l’organisation et de la gestion d’une cuisine professionnelle, conformément aux objectifs de votre cursus.

En tant que chef ou cheffe de clinique, vous avez obtenu votre titre de spécialiste en infectiologie ou êtes sur le point de finaliser votre formation.
Dans cette fonction, vous assurez l’ensemble des activités cliniques du service et évoluez dans un environnement universitaire stimulant, à l’interface des soins, de l’enseignement et de la recherche. Grâce à votre expertise clinique et à votre capacité d’adaptation, vous intervenez dans les secteurs et unités du service suivant : la consultation d’infectiologie générale, la consultation d’infectiologie ambulatoire, l’orthopédie septique, le HIV, l’infectiologie gériatrique, ainsi que l’infectiologie des patients immunodéprimés.
Sous la supervision d’un médecin adjoint, vous assurez de manière autonome l’évaluation, le diagnostic et le suivi de situations cliniques souvent complexes, tout en apportant un appui spécialisé aux équipes médico-soignantes. Vous mobilisez votre sens clinique, votre esprit d’analyse et votre capacité de décision afin de garantir une prise en charge de qualité, fondée sur les meilleures pratiques médicales.
Grâce à votre sens de l’organisation et à votre aptitude à gérer les priorités, vous conduisez efficacement vos activités cliniques tout en répondant aux nombreuses sollicitations liées à votre fonction (patients et patientes, téléphones, correspondances, réunions). Vous veillez au respect des procédures institutionnelles et contribuez activement à l’amélioration continue de la qualité et de la sécurité des soins.
Face à des situations exigeantes et à la diversité des problématiques rencontrées, vous faites preuve de discernement, de résilience et d’une excellente gestion du stress. Votre curiosité intellectuelle et votre intérêt pour l’évolution des connaissances médicales vous permettent de maintenir un haut niveau d’expertise.
Évoluant au sein d’une équipe pluridisciplinaire, vous collaborez étroitement avec les différents services, ainsi que les professionnels et professionnelles de l’institution dans une approche coordonnée et centrée sur les besoins des patientes et patients. Vous entretenez des relations de travail constructives et favorisez une communication claire, respectueuse et adaptée avec vos collègues, les personnes prises en charge et leurs proches.
En vous appuyant sur votre esprit d’équipe, vous faites preuve de solidarité face aux imprévus. En tant que cheffe ou chef de clinique, vous participez activement à la supervision et à la formation des médecins internes du service, en adoptant une posture de mentorat et en partageant votre expertise.
Par ailleurs, vous avez la possibilité de participer à des projets de recherche en cours au sein du service.

À la Clinique de Crans-Montana, l’équipe du service hôtelier contribue chaque jour au confort, à l’accueil et au bien-être des patientes et patients. Elle assure l’entretien des chambres et des locaux selon les normes d’hygiène hospitalière en vigueur, participe au service des repas en salle à manger et à la cafétéria, et veille à offrir un environnement agréable et de qualité.
En tant qu’apprentie ou apprenti gestionnaire en hôtellerie-intendance, vous êtes amené ou amenée à découvrir et à exercer de nombreuses activités au sein de différents secteurs de l’institution. Vous participez aux travaux de nettoyage et d’entretien, au service des repas et des boissons, à la gestion du linge, à l’accueil des patients à la réception ainsi qu’à certaines activités de préparation en cuisine. Vous réalisez également diverses tâches administratives, notamment liées à la gestion des stocks et aux commandes.
La diversité des missions proposées et les exigences propres au milieu hospitalier vous permettent de bénéficier d’une formation complète et variée, favorisant le développement de compétences tant techniques que relationnelles. Afin d’enrichir votre parcours, des stages externes sont organisés pour vous permettre de découvrir d’autres domaines d’activité, notamment la gestion professionnelle d’une lingerie.
Au fil de votre apprentissage, vous développez votre sens du service, votre autonomie et votre polyvalence, tout en acquérant les compétences nécessaires à l’exercice du métier, conformément aux objectifs de votre formation.

En tant que médecin interne, vous avez débuté votre parcours de formation en médecine interne et souhaitez désormais vous orienter vers l’obtention du titre de spécialiste en infectiologie.
Dans ce contexte, vous rejoignez le Service des maladies infectieuses et participez aux activités des différentes consultations spécialisées, notamment en maladies infectieuses générales, auprès des personnes immunodéprimées, des personnes âgées, dans le domaine de l’orthopédie septique et du VIH/Sida, au travers de rotations.
Sous la supervision des médecins cadres, vous assurez la prise en charge des patientes et patients qui vous sont confiés, tant en ambulatoire qu’en intrahospitalier, au sein de l’ensemble de l’institution. Vous développez progressivement votre expertise clinique en étant confronté et confrontée à des situations variées et parfois complexes, qui renforcent vos capacités d’analyse, votre jugement clinique et votre aptitude à vous adapter rapidement à de nouveaux contextes médicaux.
Grâce à votre sens de l’organisation et à votre rigueur, vous assurez les activités cliniques, diagnostiques et thérapeutiques nécessaires à la prise en charge des patientes et patients. Vous veillez au respect des règles et des procédures internes, dans un souci constant de qualité des prestations médicales apportées.
Face à la diversité des demandes de consultation et à la complexité de certaines situations cliniques, vous faites preuve de sang-froid, de discernement et d’une bonne gestion du stress. Votre curiosité intellectuelle vous incite à approfondir vos connaissances et à comprendre les enjeux des situations auxquelles vous faites face. Vous accueillez également les retours constructifs avec ouverture et les utilisez comme leviers de progression dans l’atteinte de vos objectifs de formation.
Évoluant dans un environnement universitaire stimulant et exigeant, au sein d’une équipe pluridisciplinaire, vous participez également à la formation des médecins stagiaires. Vous collaborez étroitement avec l’ensemble des équipes médico-soignantes de l’institution, dans une approche proactive et centrée sur les besoins des patientes et patients. Vous veillez à maintenir une communication claire, respectueuse et adaptée, tant avec vos collègues qu’avec les personnes prises en charge et leurs proches.
Par ailleurs, vous avez la possibilité de participer à des projets de recherche en cours au sein du service.
Dans le cadre de votre parcours de formation, vous développez vos compétences conformément au plan de formation et aux exigences de la FMH durant trois années au sein du service. Celui-ci offre un environnement reconnu pour la qualité de son enseignement, un large éventail d’activités en infectiologie ainsi que des opportunités de développement favorisant l’obtention du titre FMH. Vous bénéficiez également d’un accompagnement personnalisé grâce à des séances de coaching, des formations ciblées et un encadrement régulier assuré par les médecins cadres ainsi que les chefs et cheffes de clinique.

Dans le cadre de votre fonction, vous assurez le bon fonctionnement des systèmes informatiques du Département de Médecine.
Vous assurez la gestion et le suivi des demandes ainsi que le suivi du renouvellement du parc informatique du Département de Médecine en lien avec la DTN-IA.
Vous coordonnez avec l’équipe des correspondants informatiques les maintenances, mises à jour, upgrades de versions, migrations des logiciels du département avec les éditeurs externes et internes notamment avec les référents applicatifs des services, la DTN-IA et le service biomédical.
Vous assurez l’assistance aux utilisateurs et utilisatrices du département.
Vous participez à l’élaboration de statistiques.

Au sein de l'équipe RH du Département de médecine interne, votre activité englobe notamment la gestion administrative des collaboratrices et collaborateurs dudit département incluant la production d’actes administratifs variés.
Dans le cadre de cette opportunité, vous renseignez et conseillez les collaboratrices et collaborateurs et les cadres sur les questions liées aux procédures RH et vous assumez la gestion administrative pour le public cible dont vous êtes responsable, ceci en synergie avec deux collègues responsables RH adjointes et deux gestionnaires RH. Ainsi, vous intervenez au plan administratif sur tout le cycle de vie des membres du personnel, du recrutement au départ, et en lien avec de nombreux partenaires de la DRH et de l’institution (gestionnaire salaire, service recrutement, managers, etc.). 
Vous garantissez, par délégation du responsable des ressources humaines, l'organisation et la gestion des activités liées au traitement des dossiers tout en veillant à une juste répartition des priorités. Vous coordonnez les prestations RH selon les règles et directives de la DRH en représentant la politique des ressources humaines institutionnelle.
Vous apportez du soutien à votre responsable dans le développement d’un climat de travail harmonieux et respectueux des personnes.
Personne orientée service clients et solutions, vous vous reconnaissez par ailleurs dans les valeurs des HUG que vous incarnez dans l’exercice de vos fonctions.

Job Description SummaryRole Type: Onsite Working, #LI-Onsite
Location: Basel, Switzerland
Relocation Support: This role is based in Basel, Switzerland. Novartis is unable to offer relocation support: please only apply if accessible.

What if your expertise in structural biology could reveal the molecular insights that unlock the next generation of medicines? As Principal Scientist/Senior Scientist, Cryogenic Electron Microscopy (Cryo-EM) Structural Biology, you will join the Protein Sciences group within Discovery Sciences, applying cutting-edge Cryo-EM to challenging targets across early drug discovery. Working with scientists across Biomedical Research, you will prepare biological samples, generate and interpret high-quality structural data, and translate molecular insights into actionable science that supports the discovery of novel therapeutic candidates.

 
Job Description
Key Responsibilities:
Contribute experimentally and scientifically to early drug-discovery projects within multidisciplinary teams.
Prepare biological samples for Cryo-EM, including data collection, processing, structural determination, and model building.
Apply current Cryo-EM technologies and methodologies to generate high-quality structural insights for drug discovery.
Collaborate closely with laboratory associates, providing mentoring and technical training within a matrix environment.
Maintain accurate experimental records, scientific documentation, and instrument logs to support data quality and reproducibility.
Communicate structural biology findings through internal and external presentations and scientific publications.

Essential Requirements:
PhD in a relevant scientific discipline with at least five years of research experience, or an equivalent combination of training and experience.
Deep expertise in Cryo-EM, including sample preparation, single-particle analysis, structure determination, model building, and structural interpretation.
Hands-on experience operating high-end cryo-transmission electron microscopes.
Demonstrated experience in the expression and purification of a range of protein targets.
Excellent written and spoken English, with strong scientific communication and presentation skills.
Strong analytical skills, attention to detail, and a collaborative approach to working within multidisciplinary scientific teams.

Desirable Requirements:
Experience troubleshooting and optimizing experimental and data-processing workflows for single-particle analysis and cryo-electron tomography.
Familiarity with artificial intelligence-based and computational tools for protein construct design and optimization.
Experience characterizing protein-ligand interactions.
Hands-on experience with single-particle analysis, cryo-electron tomography, and dual-beam scanning electron microscopy.

Why Novartis:
At Novartis, you will join a collaborative Protein Sciences team applying complementary technologies, including biophysics, Nuclear Magnetic Resonance spectroscopy, X-ray crystallography, and Cryo-Electron Microscopy, to advance target-based drug discovery and novel therapeutic candidates.

Benefits & Rewards:
At Novartis, we’re committed to reimagining medicine together - and rewarding the people who make it happen.

Expected Annual Base Salary Range for role: 93,800.00 - 174,200.00 CHF

The base salary offered is determined based on gender-neutral objectives, such as relevant skills, competencies and experience in accordance with the Novartis pay setting policy and upon joining Novartis will be reviewed periodically.

In addition to your base salary, you may be eligible for a performance-based bonus depending on certain performance parameters.
The rewards of being part of our team go far beyond base pay and incentives.

We also offer a variety of competitive benefits in kind to help you thrive personally and professionally, such as insurance plans, retirement plans, wellbeing resources and global recognition programs. In addition, we provide flexible and hybrid working options, where possible, and minimum 14 weeks paid parental leave. 

Read our brochure to learn more about our global total rewards offering:
https://www.novartis.com/sites/novartis_com/files/novartis-life-handbook.pdf

Note: Benefits and compensation may vary by country and are subject to local legal requirements, including provisions of collective bargaining agreements where applicable. A full overview of your compensation package, including any relevant collective bargaining agreement details applicable to your role based on your employment location and Novartis employer entity, will be communicated separately to you during the application process.

Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion / EEO paragraph:
Novartis is committed to building an outstanding, inclusive work environment and diverse teams’ representative of the patients and communities we serve.

 
Skills DesiredAnalytical Chemistry, Analytical Laboratory Equipment, Analytical Thinking, Chemical Analysis, Chemistry, Data Capturing, Data Science, Digital Workflows, Employee Development, Employee Performance Management, High-Performance Liquid Chromatography (HPLC), Laboratory Automation, Life Sciences R&D, Machine Learning (ML), Physicochemical Characterization, Python (Programming Language), Scientific Publications, Spectrometry, Spectroscopy, Therapeutic Modalities

The BE-EA-DC section is responsible of mechanical beamline equipment such as beam intercepting devices and beam instrumentations. This equipment requires constant maintenance and upgrading to ensure its reliability and accuracy.
Your responsibilities
Conduct the dismantling/assembling activities of the beam line equipment.
Actively participate in all stages of the mechanical equipment readiness, from production to installation.
Collaborate closely with engineers, coordination teams, technicians.
Communicate and report the advancement of the work to the supervisor and project managers.
Participate to various mechanical design studies (new beam line equipment, tooling, upgrade).
Write technical specifications and procedures (maintenance, installation).
Maintain up to date and improve the equipment maintenance database.
More information here.

Hands-on experience with mechanical equipment assembly and installation.
Experience reading 2D drawings (ISO-GPS).
Familiarity with 3D modeling software (CATIA) and Microsoft Office pack.

Skills

Knowledge of manufacturing methods and work preparation (procedures, orders, BOM, metrology, logistics... ).

Do you enjoy building, assembling and bringing machines to life?
Join CERN and contribute to the development of advanced electro-mechanical equipment used in a unique high-technology environment. Working alongside experienced engineers and technicians, you will take part in the design, assembly, wiring, testing and commissioning of specialised machines, gaining hands-on experience across electrical, mechanical and control systems.
We will provide all the training you need. What matters most is your curiosity, practical mindset, and eagerness to learn.
Your responsibilities
Learn how to inspect and test advanced materials, carrying out quality checks and measurements to ensure they meet specifications.
Support laboratory testing activities and help evaluate how materials behave under different mechanical conditions.
Gain hands-on experience in creating electrical diagrams, wiring equipment, programming PLCs, and commissioning electro-mechanical machines.
Participate in the assembly, testing and operation of specialised machinery used in a cutting-edge engineering environment.
Work with experienced engineers and technicians to integrate new materials into innovative cables and coils for future technologies.

Basic experience in electrical testing or material testing.
Basic experience in reading and drawing of circuit diagrams.
Experience in the cabling and commissioning of electrical cabinets or machines is an advantage.
Experience in mechanical assembly is an advantage.
Skills
Knowledge in instrumentation and data acquisition is an advantage.
Able to work independently and in teams.
Reliable and autonomous.
Spoken and written English or French, with a commitment to learn the other language.

The successful candidate will join an innovative Antibody Discovery and Engineering department with a strong record of success in developing novel antibody therapeutics in the field of immune-oncology and autoimmune diseases. We are looking for a motivated and talented scientist with deep understanding and strong hands-on experience in antibody display technologies, antibody expression and biophysical characterization to support the discovery of next generation MultispecificTM antibodies.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

Contribute to the development of antibody discovery platform by designing and generating novel antibody libraries for phage, yeast or mammalian display applications.

Lead and perform antibody discovery campaign using phage, yeast or mammalian display.

Perform high-throughput screening of antibodies using techniques such as surface plasmon resonance (SPR), ELISA, or flow cytometry.

DNA sequence analysis of selected antibodies (Sanger or NGS)

Clone, express, and purify therapeutic antibodies.

Characterize antibody candidates using analytical methods (e.g. SDS-PAGE, SEC, DSF, AC-SINS, polyreactivity) and flow-cytometry.

Develop and perform protein-protein interaction assays, including kinetic, epitope binning, blocking assays (ELISA, SPR, BLI)

Participate in streamlining antibody discovery processes by implementing new technologies and adopting AI/ML.

Effectively support projects and accomplish goals under project timelines.

Interface with multiple discovery project and matrix teams across the organization

Effectively communicate research progress and opportunities to senior management

Support a culture that embraces scientific excellence, continuous learning, and increasing team’s ability to deliver novel drug candidates

 

 

EDUCATION AND DESIRED EXPERIENCE:

 

Ph.D. entry level or MSc degree in biotechnology, biochemistry or related discipline is required. At least 5 years of relevant industrial experience is preferred.

Hands-on experience with protein engineering using display systems (phage, yeast or mammalian display) is required.

Proficiency in molecular biology techniques (RNA extraction, RT-PCR, PCR, cloning, primer design) and DNA sequence analysis software is required.

Experience with protein expression and characterization (e.g.  SDS-PAGE, SEC) is required.

Experience with protein-protein interaction technologies (e.g. SPR/BLI) would be a plus.

Strong English communication skills, both oral and written

Rigorous, excellent organization skills, autonomous, hands-on and team minded

Strong interpersonal communication skills and the ability to present to all levels of the organization

Proven experience in problem analysis/solving

Proactive, reactive and adaptable

LOCATION:
You will join us, a vibrant biotech community at the Biopôle (https://www.biopole.ch/) overlooking the beautiful shores of Geneva lake in Lausanne, Switzerland.

/job/Basel/Senior-Machine-Learning-Scien.description:
At Roche you can show up as yourself, embraced for the unique qualities you bring. Our culture encourages personal expression, open dialogue, and genuine connections,  where you are valued, accepted and respected for who you are, allowing you to thrive both personally and professionally. This is how we aim to prevent, stop and cure diseases and ensure everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Join Roche, where every voice matters.

The Position
A healthier future. It’s what drives us to innovate. To continuously advance science and ensure everyone has access to the healthcare they need today and for generations to come. Creating a world where we all have more time with the people we love. That’s what makes us Roche.
Advances in AI, data, and computational sciences are transforming drug discovery and development. Roche’s Research and Early Development organisations at Genentech (gRED) and Pharma (pRED) have demonstrated how these technologies accelerate R&D, leveraging data and novel computational models to drive impact. Seamless data sharing and access to models across gRED and pRED are essential to maximising these opportunities. The new Computational Sciences Center of Excellence (CoE) is a strategic, unified group whose goal is to harness the transformative power of data and Artificial Intelligence (AI) to assist our scientists in both pRED and gRED to deliver more innovative and transformative medicines for patients worldwide. ​

Frontier Research is dedicated to foundational machine learning research and developing new algorithmic frameworks. We operate with a flat scientific structure in which senior scientists define their own research agendas, and leaders act as mentors who shape priorities across the organization. We view open science as a core value and a competitive necessity. Our commitment to open dissemination, academic engagement, and community contribution ensures that our work contributes meaningfully to the broader machine learning community and advances the scientific ecosystem.  In biology, many exciting research questions cannot yet be addressed with off-the-shelf ML approaches—they demand not only novel solutions but also new ways of framing the questions themselves, often beyond existing ML paradigms. We believe that the field of generative modeling provides the most promising paths to connect these fields and build robust, impactful solutions.

The Opportunity:

Design, implement, and benchmark novel machine learning algorithms grounded in causal representation learning and out-of-distribution generalization to address complex biological problems.
Frame foundational research questions that transcend off-the-shelf ML paradigms, creating robust, deployable architectures tailored to drug discovery.
Partner and collaborate closely with cross-functional research teams across our global innovation hubs in Basel, New York, and San Francisco.
Build, experiment with, and scale unconventional neural network architectures using standard deep learning frameworks.
Translate abstract biological challenges into rigorous computational models capable of bridging the gap between machine learning theory and clinical impact.
Author and drive high-impact scientific publications for submission to top-tier machine learning and computational biology venues.
Present research findings and represent the Frontier Research team at both internal symposia and leading international scientific conferences.
Actively engage in knowledge-sharing, code reviews, and technical discussions that elevate our computational capabilities and foster an open, innovative team dynamic.

Who you are:

Currently pursuing a Ph.D. (or exceptional Master's degree) in Computer Science, Statistics, Applied Mathematics, Computational Biology, Physics, or a closely related technical field, with strong practical research experience.
Solid grounding in machine learning theory and principles, with practical familiarity or strong interest in causal representation learning and/or out-of-distribution generalization.
Hands-on expertise in building, training, and troubleshooting deep neural networks, with demonstrated proficiency in modern deep learning frameworks (PyTorch strongly preferred).
Demonstrated track record of scientific contribution, evidenced by publications or accepted manuscripts at premier machine learning conferences or journals (e.g., NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, AISTATS, UAI, CVPR, ACL).
Exposure to or strong interest in working with biological datasets and molecular systems (prior direct biological experience is an asset, but not mandatory).
Outstanding collaborative and interpersonal skills, capable of communicating intricate technical ideas clearly across multi-disciplinary, distributed global teams.
Driven by curiosity, unconventional problem-solving, and a commitment to core values of Integrity, Courage, and Passion.

Ready to bring your unique qualities to Roche and make an impact? Apply now and join us in our mission to shape the future of healthcare.

 
 Where pay transparency applies, details are provided based on the primary posting location. For this role, the primary location is Basel. If you are interested in additional locations where the role may be available, we will provide the relevant compensation details later in the hiring process.

Who we are
A healthier future drives us to innovate. Together, more than 100’000 employees across the globe are dedicated to advance science, ensuring everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Our efforts result in more than 26 million people treated with our medicines and over 30 billion tests conducted using our Diagnostics products. We empower each other to explore new possibilities, foster creativity, and keep our ambitions high, so we can deliver life-changing healthcare solutions that make a global impact.

Let’s build a healthier future, together.

Roche is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

/job/Basel/Clinical-Pharmacology-Lead---.description:
At Roche you can show up as yourself, embraced for the unique qualities you bring. Our culture encourages personal expression, open dialogue, and genuine connections,  where you are valued, accepted and respected for who you are, allowing you to thrive both personally and professionally. This is how we aim to prevent, stop and cure diseases and ensure everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Join Roche, where every voice matters.

The Position
In Roche’s Pharmaceutical Research and Early Development organisation (pRED), we make transformative medicines for patients in order to tackle some of the world’s toughest unmet healthcare needs. At pRED, we are united by our mission to transform science into medicines. Together, we create a culture defined by curiosity, responsibility, and humility, where our talented people are empowered and inspired to bring forward extraordinary, life-changing innovation at speed.

At the intersection of science and innovation, pRED’s Pharmaceutical Sciences (PS) organisation enables the discovery and development of safe and effective therapeutics at optimal doses in relevant populations with a vision to power translation, continuously improve the accuracy of our predictions and accelerate the development of tomorrow's medicines. By seamlessly integrating our three core pillars—Translational Safety, Translational Pharmacology, and Biomarkers—we drive end-to-end asset development across the entire value chain, from target assessment to on-market support. Our mission is to continuously improve predictive accuracy, optimise dosing strategies for the right patient populations, and accelerate the development of tomorrow's safe and effective therapeutics. 

Within the Clinical Pharmacology Section in the Quantitative Clinical Pharmacology Department, this position operates globally, is deeply embedded within cross-functional matrix project teams and can support multiple of Roche's focus disease areas (CVRM, Immunology, Neuroscience, Oncology and Ophthalmology).

The Opportunity

In this role, you will lead the scientific advancement of clinical programs by serving as the core quantitative and clinical pharmacology lead within cross-functional project teams. You will drive all aspects of Clinical Pharmacology (CP) across all development phases and strategically apply Model-Informed Drug Development (MIDD) approaches to optimise trial designs, justify dose selections, inform development decisions and mitigate risks across both early and late-stage development. Your scope will be modality-agnostic, giving you oversight that spans small molecules, large molecules, and novel platforms. 

Strategic & Quantitative Plan Execution: Actively contribute to the development of clinical development strategies, including the design of clinical trials and lead the development, implementation, and execution of the Clinical Pharmacology and MIDD strategies for assigned assets across all development phases. Translate Clinical Pharmacology principles into predictive models that guide dose/regimen selection, drug-drug interactions (DDI), special population strategies, pediatric extrapolations and geographic/ethnic bridging.
Modelling & Simulation Mastery: Apply pharmacometric methodologies (such as population PK/PD, PBPK, or QSP) to perform clinical trial simulations, characterise exposure-response relationships, and define quantitative criteria for early, data-driven go/no-go decisions. You bring proficiency in pharmacometric software (e.g., NONMEM, R, SimCyp, MATLAB). 
Regulatory & Asset Maximisation: Lead the CP sections of major regulatory documents (including IB, IND, PIP, PSP, NDA, BLA). Ensure high-quality, fit-for-purpose submission documents using Roche initiatives like lean development authoring and digital submission excellence. Represent the company as a subject matter expert in health authority interactions.
Business Development: Provide clinical and quantitative pharmacology expertise during due diligence for in-licensing and out-licensing activities.
Digital Innovation: Proactively develop and incorporate AI/ML methodologies into Clinical Pharmacology activities and day-to-day quantitative workflows to optimise data interpretation and efficiency.
Matrix Influence & Resilience: Work effectively across a complex, global matrix organisation. Address conflicts with high resilience and foster an environment of challenger safety where diverse scientific views are valued.
Mentorship: Guide and mentor junior scientists within the department to foster strategic and technical growth and professional development.

 
Who You Are

Education: You hold a PhD, Pharm.D., or MD with a specialisation in Pharmacometrics, Clinical Pharmacology, or a related scientific discipline.
Experience: You bring 5+ years of experience in the pharmaceutical or biotech industry in the area of Quantitative Clinical Pharmacology. You have a strong understanding of drug discovery and clinical development, including biology and disease knowledge, and you bring a proven track record of applying Model-Informed Drug Development (MIDD) principles. 
Technical Toolkit: You have a strong foundation in Clinical Pharmacology principles and quantitative drug development, with a solid understanding and experience in applying advanced quantitative modelling (proven proficiency in core pharmacometric software/tool kits such as NONMEM, R or Simcyp), data analytics, and emerging AI-enabled approaches to support evidence-based decision-making. You understand the regulatory landscape and how to integrate diverse data to optimise development.
Communication: You have outstanding communication skills and a clear ability to translate complex quantitative data into actionable strategic messages for cross-functional leadership.
Matrix Influence & Resilience:  You demonstrate strategic thinking,  matrix flexibility and high resilience, working effectively across global organisations to handle conflicts and foster an environment of challenger safety where diverse scientific views are valued.

At Roche, we aim high to deliver life-changing healthcare solutions. If you’re ready to make a meaningful impact on patients and healthcare systems worldwide, this is the place for you.

 
 Where pay transparency applies, details are provided based on the primary posting location. For this role, the primary location is Basel. If you are interested in additional locations where the role may be available, we will provide the relevant compensation details later in the hiring process.

Who we are
A healthier future drives us to innovate. Together, more than 100’000 employees across the globe are dedicated to advance science, ensuring everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Our efforts result in more than 26 million people treated with our medicines and over 30 billion tests conducted using our Diagnostics products. We empower each other to explore new possibilities, foster creativity, and keep our ambitions high, so we can deliver life-changing healthcare solutions that make a global impact.

Let’s build a healthier future, together.

Roche is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

/job/Warsaw/Data-Scientist_202609-122958.description:
At Roche you can show up as yourself, embraced for the unique qualities you bring. Our culture encourages personal expression, open dialogue, and genuine connections,  where you are valued, accepted and respected for who you are, allowing you to thrive both personally and professionally. This is how we aim to prevent, stop and cure diseases and ensure everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Join Roche, where every voice matters.

The Position
Data Scientist

Roche Digital Technology (RDT) is where innovation meets purpose. 

As a global team at the heart of Roche, we are a community of business-minded technologists committed to help shape tomorrow’s digital future of healthcare. Our mission is to power Roche through cutting-edge digital technologies, harnessing the potential of artificial intelligence, data, and scalable tech innovations. Driven by purpose and passion, we’re building a future where digital is a core strength across all of Roche, enabling smarter ways of working, unlocking human potential, and driving breakthroughs that truly matter for millions of patients around the world. 

You'll work alongside curious, ambitious technologists who value ownership, rigour, and fast, visible impact over process for its own sake. Rather than settling into one fixed lane, you'll move with the work as priorities shift, growing your expertise across a genuinely wide range of problems. If you want your day-to-day work to reach millions of patients and to help shape what a still-emerging technology looks like in practice, this is a rare moment to join at the ground floor.

At Roche, we offer a hybrid work model that combines flexibility with in-person collaboration. For now, we require our employees to be in our Warsaw or Poznań office on average two days per week. The specific office days may vary depending on business needs, such as workshops, conferences, town halls, team meetings, and other collaborative events.

The opportunity: 

Roche's AI Function builds the platforms, tools, and data science muscle that let teams across Roche turn AI, GenAI, and agentic ideas into real products, fast. We make it safe, simple, and scalable to build with LLMs, enterprise data, and orchestration, so experimentation stops staying experimental and starts driving real business value. And now we're pushing further into agentic AI: systems that reason, plan, and act on their own, under human oversight. Join us and help define how Roche builds, evaluates, and governs that next generation of AI at enterprise scale.

The kind of work you'll do 
Build and ship
Design and ship AI/ML solutions, from prototype to a monitored capability people actually depend on, including Roche's next generation of agentic AI: systems that plan and execute complex, multi-step work autonomously. Work closely with product owners, engineers, and business stakeholders throughout.
Turn ambiguous problems into clear modelling approaches, and explain the trade-offs in language anyone can follow. Choose the right tool for the problem: a classical model, a fine-tuned model, retrieval over a foundation model or an agentic workflow, rather than reaching for an LLM by default.
Write clean, production-ready, reproducible code, and help shape the reusable patterns the wider team relies on.
Bring rigour
Bring rigour to every experiment. Solid baselines, held-out testing, real error analysis. No shortcuts.
Treat evaluation as core craft, not an afterthought. Build eval sets and harnesses for GenAI systems, use golden datasets and regression checks for prompts, and statistically evaluate outputs for safety, reliability and consistency, offline and in production.
Root solutions in real user feedback, not just lab results.
Measure and inform
Power decisions with analytics. Surface the cost, value, adoption, and usage data that tells AI leadership what's working and where to invest next.
Govern and share
Build within Roche's governance, security, and compliance guardrails, from day one of a project to the last.
Contribute to those guardrails in practice: help design the checks that help embed fairness, explainability and privacy into pipelines so they are enforced rather than aspirational.
Share what you learn through reviews, demos, and onboarding docs. No lesson stays siloed.

Who you are :

Technical depth
Hands-on expertise in data science and software engineering. Python, LLMs, RAG pipelines, agentic workflows. Equally comfortable writing production code, designing system architecture, or setting integration standards.
Evaluate and fine-tune pre-trained models for domain use. Design RAG and search/synthesis architectures. Build evaluation harnesses and statistically evaluate outputs for safety, reliability, and consistency.
Strong NLP foundations: preprocessing, language modelling, sentiment analysis, NER.
A solid core in statistics, model evaluation, feature engineering and standard algorithms
Real depth on vector embeddings, search theory, and vector database selection and architecture, along with prompt and context engineering.

Strategic and operational range
Comfortable moving from strategic roadmap planning to solving ad-hoc technical problems on the ground. Skilled at bridging non-technical stakeholders and technical implementation.
Comfortable building MLOps/LLMOps pipelines for continuous deployment and monitoring, including observability for LLM systems (tracing, tokens, latency, cost telemetry and drift and hallucination monitoring). 
Comfortable forecasting and optimising infrastructure and API costs, and managing platform vendor relationships to keep tools interoperable, secure, and future-proof.
Communication
Strong written and verbal English, with the ability to explain technical trade-offs to technical and non-technical audiences alike.
A learning posture that keeps pace with a fast-changing field, with enthusiasm for knowledge-sharing.  
Preferred/nice to have:
Hands-on experience deploying enterprise AI solutions on AWS or Azure (GCP exposure a plus).
Model risk management, fairness and bias mitigation, transparency, explainability, and data privacy.
Pharma, healthcare, or financial services, including GxP compliance and handling sensitive information, plus awareness of emerging compliance standards for GenAI and foundation models.

What You Get
Salary Range: 170’100.00 - 243’000.00 - 315’900.00 PLN Annual based on an employment contract (Umowa o Pracę).
Annual Performance Bonus: Target bonus of 15% based on performance.
Dedicated Training Budget: Funding for certifications, AI/tech courses, global conferences, and diversified career paths.
Recharge Fridays: 2 additional paid Fridays off per quarter available to completely disconnect.

Who we are:

We, the Digital Biomarker (dBM) and Remote Patient Management (RPM) Chapter in Roche Information Solutions, are an integrated team of scientists, technologists, data analysts and operations experts, that leverages mobile technologies like smartphones and wearables to  bring the power of sensor measures to patients everywhere: in clinical drug trials and clinical care.
We drive research, workflows and analytics for Digital Biomarkers and Remote patient management in Roche Information Solutions. Together with our partners, we invent, design and deliver solution capabilities, products and services for better clinical research and improved healthcare outcomes. We are establishing the scientific foundations for disease monitoring and screening solutions in clinical practice and enable patients and healthcare providers to leverage the power of sensor data for better outcomes in the management of neurological disease, diabetes and others. 

Here’s what we’re looking for:

Are you passionate about leveraging digital health technology (DHT) to revolutionize healthcare? At Roche, we are seeking a dedicated Digital Biomarker Science & Technology Neuroscience Lead to join our Digital Biomarker (dBM) and Remote Patient Management (RPM) Chapter. Based on a deep understanding of clinical trials in neurology in general and deep customer insights, you ensure that we meet the evolving needs of our BioPharma customers and their clinical trials.
You will shape the internal and external scientific communication of our products’ value propositions, actively engaging with prospective customers in a pre-sales capacity to translate complex scientific data into compelling solution strategies.  Together with the scientific community, you will drive the acceptance of sensor-based outcome measures. acting as an influential scientific thought leader in the network of academia, industry, the patient community and regulators.  Internally at Roche, you will lead cross-functional squads to develop and execute on the scientific product vision. As such, you will closely work with experts in the dBM & RPM chapter, cross-functional stakeholders across Roche Diagnostics and Pharma Global & Affiliate organizations. 

Who You are:

Collaborate with the International Product Manager for Chronic Remote Care Management to leverage scientific data insights and customer feedback to discover, develop and scale a product that is desirable, feasible and viable.
Together with the International Product Manager for Chronic Remote Care Management, develop and cultivate networks with key opinion leaders for Neuroscience as well as with key stakeholders within the company.
Partner with a broad stakeholder community of patients, care givers, physician and other experts to create scientific digital health solutions 
Act as scientific product owner for a set of digital biomarker solutions for Roche and external customers with needs in areas of Disease understanding / Drug portfolio decision-making (phase I-II) / Regulatory treatment approval (phase III-IV) / Clinical trial participant selection / Clinical care
Oversee end-to-end scientific product research & development and the scientific roadmap
Scientifically lead large interdisciplinary project teams that identify, design, develop and implement the scientific digital biomarker solutions to address the unmet measurement needs
Drive the regulatory strategy for digital endpoint endorsement and qualification
Drive scientific community acceptance of digital measures and maintain a strong network of collaborators spanning industry and academia
Develop scientific core messages for product marketing
Represent RIS scientifically in pre-sales conversations on Remote Patient Management and  Digital Biomarker products
Plan, initiate and co-author high-profile scientific publications and posters and represent Roche at relevant high-profile conferences
Grow your influence as a respected scientific digital biomarker expert and advocate in the research and development community at Roche and externally through cross-industry task forces, communicating results at conferences and in peer-reviewed publications.
Drive the scientific foundations of clinical use scenarios based on sensor-measurements to improve outcomes for patients as well as the efficiency of healthcare delivery

Who you are:

University degree  (Ph.D. or equivalent) in Life Sciences or related field with a minimum of 10 years related experience in the pharmaceutical and digital health industry 
Track record of writing compelling publications in high impact, peer-reviewed journals
Proven experience with senior stakeholder management and external collaborations
Deep scientific product management experience in a large Pharma or Medtech company 
Deep experience in the area of sensor data and digital biomarker development
Provable experience leading in a matrix setup, recognized for embracing new ways of leading and working, with strengths in coaching and fostering a collaborative environment
Transparent communicator and able to apply effective empowering leadership
Previous clinical experience in chronic disease management and Neuroscience (especially Parkinson’s Disease, Huntington’s Disease, Multiple Sclerosis)

Should you have these additional nice-to-have skills, you are the ideal team member we are searching for:

Comprehensive understanding of the current state of drug development for Parkinson's and Huntington's Disease
In-depth knowledge of the clinical endpoint landscape and associated challenges in Parkinson's and Huntington's Disease
Overview of existing digital biomarker approaches for these diseases 
Experience with developing digital outcome measures
FDA/EMA regulatory interactions or regulatory consortias regarding clinical drug development and novel drug development endpoints
