The Position
Join the small-molecule team within AI for Drug Discovery (AI4DD), formerly Prescient Design, at Roche and Genentech’s Computational Sciences Center of Excellence as a Machine Learning Scientist / Senior Machine Learning Scientist in Quantum Chemistry. You will combine machine learning methods and quantum chemistry to build fast, accurate models that power small-molecule drug discovery. You will work with world-class computational and experimental scientists and leverage proprietary datasets and state-of-the-art compute.

The Opportunity

Create cutting-edge solutions that combine quantum chemistry and machine learning algorithm development to model small-molecule energetics and protein–ligand interactions, from conformation and reactivity to binding affinity and free energy.
Build synthetic datasets using quantum mechanics and related methods to shape novel research directions in ML.
Develop deployable pipelines that are robust, scalable and reproducible, and feed directly into molecular-design tools used across Roche.
Drive scientific impact through publications, open-source releases, and talks at internal and external conferences.
Collaborate widely with world-class computational and experimental researchers at Roche and with academic partners.

Who you are

You bring deep machine-learning expertise with a strong theoretical foundation in linear algebra, probability and optimization, and you build models from first principles.
You have hands-on quantum chemistry experience and fluency in toolkits such as Psi4, PySCF and ORCA, as well as semi-empirical methods like xTB.
You are fluent in Python and modern ML frameworks such as PyTorch or JAX.
You hold a PhD or equivalent research depth in machine learning, computational chemistry, chemical engineering or a related quantitative field such as physics or statistics.
You have a record of scientific excellence evidenced by journal and conference publications or a public portfolio of relevant projects (e.g. hosted on GitHub/GitLab).

Preferred
Experience in scientific software development, scaling ML training, and applying models to drug discovery. 
Experience generating large-scale synthetic datasets.

Location & Travel Requirements

This position must be based in either Welwyn Garden City in the United Kingdom (preferred) or Basel, Switzerland. Although this can be a hybrid role, there is an expectation of ongoing and sustained site presence, in compliance with local company site requirements.

Job Description SummaryYou will lead the enterprise people and organization agenda for Data Science and Artificial Intelligence (DSAI) across Novartis, translating our DSAI ambition into the workforce, organization, talent and capability choices needed to deliver it. Operating at the decision-making table with senior DSAI leaders and partnering across the enterprise, you will shape how we build, attract and grow critical DSAI talent, strengthen our external value proposition, and enable responsible human-AI collaboration. You will lead the enterprise DSAI OTR, including discussion at ECN level, and create the standards, governance and frameworks needed in areas such as careers, capabilities, talent and rewards, particularly where established approaches do not yet exist.

This enterprise role complements rather than replaces the Workforce Strategy Leads directly supporting DSAI teams within their units. Unit-level accountabilities remain unchanged, while this role connects across them, providing the overarching DSAI people strategy, standards and governance and enabling enterprise-level choices where these are needed.

 
Job Description
#Hybrid

This role can be based in Cambridge, East Hanover, London or Basel, please only apply to one of the appropriate location.

Key Responsibilities
Set the enterprise DSAI people and organization strategy.
Translate the DSAI ambition into an integrated, future-ready agenda across workforce, organization, leadership, culture, talent and capability. Success is evident when: enterprise priorities and accountabilities are clear, adopted across units, and translated into measurable outcomes.
Shape strategic workforce and capability choices. Use scenarios, analytics, external insight and data storytelling to anticipate demand for scarce DSAI capabilities and recommend choices on organization design, skills, capacity, location, sourcing and workforce mix. Success is evident when: critical gaps are addressed before they constrain innovation or execution.
Lead the enterprise DSAI OTR. Orchestrate the enterprise talent review, integrate perspectives across units, and present implications, choices and recommendations to ECN. Success is evident when: pivotal talent, succession, capability risks and enterprise actions are visible and actively managed.
Establish enterprise talent and career approaches. Create differentiated career development, mobility, succession and talent-allocation mechanisms suited to DSAI roles and communities. Success is evident when: Novartis can attract, develop, deploy and retain pivotal DSAI talent across organizational boundaries.
Build the external DSAI talent brand and pipeline. Strengthen Novartis’ visibility as an employer of choice through targeted engagement with universities, specialist talent networks and external forums. Build early-talent pathways that attract dual technical/scientific and DSAI expertise and develop judgement, experience and leadership capability. Success is evident when: Novartis has stronger external visibility and a sustainable pipeline of scarce DSAI talent.
Design and create enterprise DSAI standards. Build new governance, rewards approaches, career architecture, capability frameworks, talent programs and operating approaches for a field evolving faster than established internal practices. Success is evident when: scalable standards replace fragmented local approaches and remain relevant as DSAI evolves.
Connect enterprise strategy and unit execution. Define decision rights, interfaces and governance so the enterprise mandate is distinct from, and complementary to, unchanged unit-level P&O accountabilities. Success is evident when: there is no duplication or accountability gap between enterprise and unit roles.
Influence a complex enterprise stakeholder system. Partner with at least nine ECN-1 leaders across R&D, Commercial, Operations and Global Functions, the Head of GDC, unit P&O Business Partners and Expertise Hubs to resolve enterprise trade-offs without relying on formal authority. Success is evident when: leaders move beyond unit optimization and commit to enterprise decisions.
Redesign work for human-AI collaboration. Guide organization, role and workflow choices that enable responsible collaboration among people, automation and AI agents while sustaining accountability and a human-cantered employee experience. Success is evident when: adoption improves productivity, innovation and decision quality.
Coach senior leaders, shape culture and lead transformation. Challenge and coach leaders through ambiguity, build commitment to new enterprise approaches, anticipate resistance and track adoption and benefits. Success is evident when: leadership behaviour, culture and ways of working support the DSAI strategy.
 
What you’ll bring to the role
Essential Criteria
Extensive experience of progressive P&O/HR experience, including strategic partnership with executive and ECN-1 leaders in a complex global matrix.
Strong organization design, strategic workforce planning and transformation experience, including scenario development and enterprise trade-off recommendations.
Demonstrated experience creating global or enterprise-wide people strategies, standards, governance or programs, not only implementing established solutions.
Evidence of leading enterprise talent reviews, succession and capability discussions with senior executive forums.
Demonstrated ability to influence multiple senior stakeholders across business units, functions, countries and P&O disciplines without formal authority.
Fluency in people analytics and confidence with AI-enabled tools, responsible AI principles and emerging work technologies.

Desirable Criteria
Experience translating emerging technology, data science or digital strategy into workforce, organization and talent implications; direct DSAI sector experience is highly desirable.
Relevant university degree or equivalent experience required; advanced qualification in business, organization, analytics, technology or a related discipline.

Benefits & Rewards
The salary for this position is expected to range between 204,400.00 - 379,600.00 USD Annual.

The final salary offered is determined based on factors like, but not limited to, relevant skills and experience, and upon joining Novartis will be reviewed periodically. Novartis may change the published salary range based on company and market factors. Your compensation will include a performance-based cash incentive and, depending on the level of the role, eligibility to be considered for annual equity awards. US-based eligible employees will receive a comprehensive benefits package that includes health, life and disability benefits, a 401(k) with company contribution and match, and a variety of other benefits. In addition, employees are eligible for a generous time off package including vacation, personal days, holidays and other leaves.

Job Description

Partner with cross-functional teams to accelerate adoption and maximize reuse.

Simplify ways of working through standardized frameworks, improved transparency, and reduced operational complexity.
Strengthen coordination and execution across US and HYD teams. 
5. AI & Operating Model Transformation
Identify and implement opportunities to improve productivity, speed, and quality through AI, automation, and process redesign.
Drive continuous improvement of TNBA's operating model and enterprise capabilities.
Enable scalable, data-driven execution across the portfolio.

/job/CH---Visp/Associate-Principal-Scien.description:
Today, Lonza is a global leader in life sciences operating across three continents. While we work in science, there’s no magic formula to how we do it. Our greatest scientific solution is talented people working together, devising ideas that help businesses to help people. In exchange, we let our people own their careers. Their ideas, big and small, genuinely improve the world. And that’s the kind of work we want to be part of.
 
We are looking for an Associate Principal Scientist (m/f/d) to join our Mammalian Cell Culture Development team in Visp. This role combines scientific leadership with hands‑on laboratory work, driving upstream development activities and collaborating with cross‑functional teams and customers to deliver high‑quality bioprocessing solutions.
 
Key responsibilities:
Lead, design, and execute complex upstream process development activities, including small‑scale studies (up to 10 L), ensuring compliance with quality and safety standards and generating the data and documentation required to support tech transfer to Pilot and GMP facilities.
Act as subject matter expert (SME) for CHO cell culture, providing scientific guidance, troubleshooting support, and decision‑making for internal and external teams.
Build and maintain strong customer relationships through transparent communication and scientific excellence.
Design, optimize, and implement robust scale‑down and scale‑up models.
Author and review high‑quality documentation, including study plans and development reports.
Support training activities and promote knowledge‑sharing across teams.
Contribute to continuous improvement, workflow optimization, and best‑practice implementation.

Key requirements:
BSc with 7+ years or MSc with 5+ years of relevant industry experience in mammalian upstream process development.
Hands‑on expertise with CHO cell culture, including AMBR250/AMBR15, shake flasks, stirred‑tank bioreactors, and depth filtration.

#LI-NR1

• Proficient understanding and knowledge of domestic and international regulatory requirements required and knowledge of therapeutic areas in all phases of clinical development desired.

Syneos Health® is a leading fully-integrated life sciences services organization built to accelerate customer success. Discover what your 25,000 future colleagues already know:
 
Why Syneos Health
• We are passionate about developing our people, through career development and progression; supportive and engaged line management; technical and therapeutic area training; peer recognition and total rewards program.
• We are committed to building an inclusive culture – where you can authentically be yourself. Central to this is our purpose – Driven to Deliver – which captures the passion of our colleagues to show up each day and shape solutions that have the ability to dramatically impact someone’s life. 
• We are continuously building the company we all want to work for and our customers want to work with. Why? Because we know that when we bring together smart colleagues from across the world, we can shape the future of healthcare, driving impact for customers and defining the pace of patient progress. 

Job Responsibilities

This is a full-time permanent position within our FSP Team. For this role, we can consider candidates based anywhere in EMEA except Switzerland, Germany and France.

Leads the clear and accurate completion of medical writing deliverables, ensuring scientific information is presented clearly and accurately. Manages medical writing activities associated with individual studies, coordinating medical writing activities within and across departments with minimal supervision. Leads the resolution of comments from the client.
Completes a variety of documents that may include clinical study protocols and clinical study protocol amendments; clinical study reports; patient narratives; annual reports; investigator brochures; informed consents; annual reports; plain language summaries; periodic safety update reports, clinical development plans; IND submissions; integrated summary reports; NDA and eCTD submissions; journal manuscripts; and abstracts, posters, and presentations for scientific meetings.
Adheres to established regulatory standards, including, but not limited to, ICH E3 guidelines, as well as company standard operating procedures, client standards, and company and/or client approved-templates, authorship requirements, and style and formatting guides, when completing medical writing projects, on time and on budget.
Coordinates quality and editorial reviews. Ensures source documentation is managed appropriately. Leads team document reviews, and reviews documents as needed.
Acts as peer reviewer for internal team to ensure document scientific content, clarity, overall consistency, and proper format.
Reviews statistical analysis plans and table/figure/listing specifications for appropriate content, and for grammar, format, and consistency. Provides feedback to further define statistical output required and document needs.
Interacts and builds good working relations with clients, department head, and peers in data management, biostatistics, regulatory affairs, and medical affairs, as necessary, to produce writing deliverables.
Performs online clinical literature searches and complies with copyright requirements.
Identifies and proposes solutions to resolve issues, escalating as appropriate. Provides technical support, training, and consultation to department and other company staff. May contribute to development of internal materials and presentations or changes to internal process, standard practices, and capabilities.
Mentors and leads less experienced medical writers on complex projects, as necessary.
Develops deep expertise on key topics in the industry and the regulatory requirements and guidelines that affect medical writing.
Aware of budget specifications for assigned projects, working within the budgeted hours and communicating status and changes to medical writing leadership.
Completes required administrative tasks within the specified timeframes.
Performs other work-related duties as assigned.
Minimal travel may be required (less than 25%).

Qualifications:

3-5 years of relevant experience in science, technical, or medical writing.
Veeva Vault - MUST HAVE
FSP or CRO experience preferred
Tech Savy - you feel comfortable using technology
Experience working in the biopharmaceutical, device, or contract research organization industry required.
Strong understanding of FDA and ICH regulations, other regulatory guidelines, and/or good publication practices strongly required.
Experience writing relevant document types required.
Extensive knowledge of English grammar and ability to communicate clearly; strong familiarity with AMA Manual of Style.

Get to know Syneos Health

Over the past 5 years, we have worked with 94% of all Novel FDA Approved Drugs, 95% of EMA Authorized Products and over 200 Studies across 73,000 Sites and 675,000+ Trial patients.

No matter what your role is, you’ll take the initiative and challenge the status quo with us in a highly competitive and ever-changing environment. Learn more about Syneos Health.

http://www.syneoshealth.com

Take the lead in regulatory affairs for OM Pharma’s Swiss portfolio, including partner products. Combining strategic ownership with hands-on delivery, you will manage a Regulatory Specialist and work closely with cross-functional teams to ensure regulatory compliance throughout the product lifecycle. Based in Villars-sur-Glâne, you will report to the Head of Market Access & External Affairs, Swiss Affiliate.

 

Your key responsibilities are as follows:

Lead regulatory strategy and operations for product development and lifecycle management across the Swiss portfolio, aligned with business objectives, timelines and budgets

Monitor regulatory developments and proactively adapt strategies to ensure compliance throughout the product lifecycle

Oversee the preparation, review and timely submission of regulatory dossiers, including variations and renewals, as applicable

Maintain regulatory databases and coordinate product information and packaging updates

Lead or support interactions with Swissmedic and other health authorities, and represent the company during quality inspections and audits

Provide regulatory expertise to cross-functional projects and align activities with key internal stakeholders

Develop or contribute to SOPs and work instructions, driving continuous improvement of regulatory processes and systems

Manage and support the Regulatory Specialist, setting objectives, coordinating daily priorities and improving team efficiency and project delivery

 

What you bring:

A university degree in Life Sciences, Pharmacy, Biomedical Sciences, Medicine or an equivalent scientific discipline

At least 5 years’ experience in Regulatory Affairs within the Swiss pharmaceutical industry, with hands-on expertise in regulatory submissions and lifecycle management, including variations and renewals

Proven experience working with Swissmedic and a solid understanding of Swiss regulatory requirements

The ability to translate complex regulatory requirements into clear, pragmatic guidance for internal stakeholders

Strong language skills: fluency in English and either French or German, with a good working knowledge of the third language; fluency in all three is preferred

You combine sound regulatory judgement with a pragmatic, hands-on and business-oriented approach. Autonomous and well-organised, you balance competing priorities without compromising quality or compliance. You build effective relationships, communicate clearly and influence stakeholders constructively. As a supportive team leader, you provide clear direction and foster collaboration and continuous improvement.

 

Ready to make a difference? Apply today and join OM Pharma in Fribourg !

 
About Us

OM Pharma is a global Geneva-based biopharmaceutical company. It is a leader in the prevention of recurrent respiratory and urinary tract infections and is also active in the treatment of vascular diseases.

It operates worldwide through a strong network of international partners and invests its profits in R&D to develop microbial derived immunotherapeutic products to treat acute and chronic immunological disorders resulting from inflammation and infections. 

The company strives to improve the quality of life of patients around the world by providing access to better treatment of immunological imbalances.

For more information, visit the website: ompharma.com.

Associate Principal Scientist – Analytical Development (Microbial)

Visp, Schweiz

Der tatsächliche Arbeitsort für diese Position ist Visp, Schweiz. Unterstützung bei der Relocation steht berechtigten Kandidaten und ihren Familien bei Bedarf zur Verfügung.

Möchten Sie die Zukunft innovativer Biopharmazeutika mitgestalten? In dieser Schlüsselrolle übernehmen Sie die wissenschaftliche und technische Verantwortung für die Entwicklung, Implementierung und Validierung moderner bioanalytischer Methoden und treiben gleichzeitig die Digitalisierung und Automatisierung analytischer Labore voran. Ihre Arbeit unterstützt direkt die Entwicklung und Herstellung innovativer biologischer Arzneimittel und ermöglicht die Bereitstellung lebensverändernder Therapien für Patienten weltweit.

Dies ist eine vollständig standortgebundene Position. Die enge Zusammenarbeit vor Ort unterstützt die direkte Abstimmung innerhalb der Teams sowie die wissenschaftliche Präzision, die erforderlich ist, um innovative Therapien nach höchsten Qualitäts- und Sicherheitsstandards zu entwickeln.

Was wir bieten

Eine agile Karriere mit vielfältigen Entwicklungsmöglichkeiten in einem internationalen Umfeld.
Eine inklusive und werteorientierte Unternehmenskultur.
Leistungsorientierte Vergütungsprogramme.
Ein attraktives Leistungs- und Benefitspaket abhängig von Rolle und Standort.
Die vollständige Übersicht unserer globalen Benefits finden Sie hier: https://www.lonza.com/careers/benefits

Ihre Aufgaben

Wissenschaftliche und technische Hauptansprechperson für die Entwicklung, Implementierung und Validierung biochemischer und chromatographischer Assays wie ELISA, Enzym-Assays, RT-qPCR, Protein-PCR, UV/Vis, icIEF sowie RP-, SE- und IEX-HPLC.
Leitung analytischer Entwicklungs-, Transfer- und Validierungsaktivitäten innerhalb mehrerer Studien- und Kundenprogramme.
Erstellung, Überprüfung und finale Freigabe komplexer Studienprotokolle, Arbeitsanweisungen und Berichte gemäß GLP-Anforderungen.
Zusammenarbeit mit funktionsübergreifenden Teams aus Analytical Development, Process Development, Manufacturing und Quality zur Sicherstellung wissenschaftlicher Exzellenz.
Training, Coaching und fachliche Weiterentwicklung von Laborfachkräften und wissenschaftlichen Mitarbeitenden.
Identifikation, Bewertung und Implementierung neuer analytischer Technologien sowie Förderung von Digitalisierungs- und Automatisierungsinitiativen.
Unterstützung kontinuierlicher Verbesserungsprozesse zur Steigerung von Effizienz, Datenqualität und regulatorischer Compliance.

Was wir suchen:

Promotion (PhD) in Biochemie, Biologie, Chemie oder einer vergleichbaren naturwissenschaftlichen Fachrichtung.
Erfahrung in der Entwicklung, Implementierung und Validierung analytischer Methoden im biopharmazeutischen oder pharmazeutischen Umfeld.
Fundierte Kenntnisse moderner bioanalytischer und chromatographischer Technologien wie ELISA, qPCR, icIEF und HPLC.
Fähigkeit, komplexe wissenschaftliche Projekte selbstständig zu leiten und technische Herausforderungen lösungsorientiert zu adressieren.
Ausgeprägte Kommunikations- und Teamfähigkeiten sowie Freude an der Zusammenarbeit in einem dynamischen Umfeld.
Hohe Eigeninitiative, Verantwortungsbewusstsein und strukturierte Arbeitsweise.
Sehr gute Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift.

Über Lonza

Bei Lonza sind unsere Mitarbeitenden unsere größte Stärke. Mit mehr als 30 Standorten auf fünf Kontinenten arbeiten unsere global vernetzten Teams täglich gemeinsam daran, die Medikamente von morgen zu entwickeln und herzustellen. Unsere Werte Collaboration, Accountability, Excellence, Passion und Integrity prägen unsere Zusammenarbeit und machen Lonza zu einem Ort, an dem jede Idee einen Unterschied machen kann.
Innovation entsteht, wenn Menschen mit unterschiedlichen Hintergründen und Perspektiven zusammenkommen. Deshalb fördern wir bei Lonza ein vielfältiges und inklusives Arbeitsumfeld, in dem alle Mitarbeitenden ihr Potenzial entfalten können.
Sind Sie bereit, die Zukunft der Life Sciences aktiv mitzugestalten und analytische Innovationen am Standort Visp voranzutreiben? Dann freuen wir uns auf Ihre Bewerbung.

Ready to shape the future of life sciences? Apply now.

En tant que stagiaire en psychologie de la santé, vous participez à différentes activités en collaboration avec un médecin et une infirmière formés en éducation thérapeutique, ainsi qu’une psychologue en poste : par exemple, l’exploration avec les patientes et les patients de leurs besoins en autogestion concernant leur condition, la participation au développement d’un itinéraire clinique de prise en charge de la goutte, l’animation d’ateliers, l’étude des perceptions et discours des patientes et des patients sur leur prise en charge de leur condition.
En collaboration avec l’ensemble de l’équipe pluridisciplinaire du service, vous participez également à la mise en place d’une stratégie de soutien à l’autogestion au service de rhumatologie, dans une dynamique de co-construction.

Comme instrumentiste, technicien ou technicienne de salle d’opération (TSO) au sein des blocs opératoires, vous assurez l’accueil et l’installation du patient ou de la patiente et vous veillez à sa sécurité.
Vous êtes responsable de préparer le matériel nécessaire à une intervention chirurgicale et de contrôler son bon fonctionnement. Vous assistez le ou la chirurgienne et vous êtes en charge des activités techniques et des soins spécifiques au bloc opératoire dans le respect des règles de bonne pratique, notamment dans le domaine de l’asepsie et des règles d’hygiène.
Votre engagement et esprit collaboratif vous permettent de contribuer activement au sein d’équipes interprofessionnelles. Vous participez activement aux réflexions visant à améliorer la qualité et la sécurité des soins.
Vous participez à l’encadrement des stagiaires, des étudiantes et étudiants au sein des blocs opératoires.
Vous aurez l’opportunité de participer à des interventions chirurgicales hautement spécialisées. Notre institution offre également de nombreuses possibilités de formation continue et une perspective de développement de carrière.

Evoluant dans un environnement technique dynamique et moderne au service de la patientèle et des collaborateurs et collaboratrices des HUG, l’équipe Systèmes Serveurs est responsable de l’administration des infrastructures hébergeant les applications métiers critiques. L’équipe est rattachée hiérarchiquement au Domaine Infrastructure du Service Opérations de la DTN-IA et travaille en étroite collaboration avec de nombreuses équipes internes, notamment en charge des Applications, des Données, de la Sécurité et du Réseau.
En tant que spécialiste Linux/containers/IA/automatisation au sein de cette équipe, vous contribuez à l’évolution du Système d’Informations en apportant des solutions techniques innovantes et en assurant la fiabilité, la sécurité et la performance des systèmes 24h/7j.
Vous concevez et administrez les serveurs virtuels et physiques Linux ainsi que les systèmes de conteneurisation et d’orchestration (idéalement Kubernetes Rancher, Docker Swarm).
Vous mettez en œuvre les outils et procédures nécessaires à une production optimale et de qualité (coûts, fiabilité, performances, surveillance, normes et standards).
Vous collaborez avec les développeurs et développeuses afin de concevoir et d’optimiser les architectures techniques en termes de résilience, performance et possibilité de croissance (scalability).
Vous assurez la mise en œuvre, le suivi des systèmes et des applications dans tout le cycle de vie des projets ainsi que la cohérence technique des solutions en collaboration avec les chefs et les cheffes de projets.
Vous participez à la rédaction des normes, standards et des procédures ainsi qu’à la veille technologique et aux actions prospectives, en vous assurant de la bonne utilisation de la base de données de gestion de la configuration (CMDB).
Vous maintenez en condition opérationnelle les moyens matériels et logiciels en veillant au respect des dates de fin de vie, des critères de performance et de sécurité. Vous analysez et gérez les incidents, vous assurez la remise en service et prenez les mesures correctives nécessaires dans une démarche d’amélioration continue.

En tant qu’infirmière ou infirmier spécialisé dans le domaine opératoire, vous assurez la prise en charge des patients et patientes durant leur séjour au sein des blocs opératoires. Vous évaluez et analysez les situations de soins complexes et dispensez des soins infirmiers de haut niveau afin de répondre aux besoins et attentes de la patientèle sur le plan techniques, relationnel et préventif. 
Votre engagement et votre esprit collaboratif vous permettent de contribuer activement au sein d’équipes interdisciplinaires. De plus, vous participez activement aux réflexions visant à optimiser la prise en charge des patientes et patients. Vous participez également à l’encadrement des étudiants et étudiantes à la formation spécialisée dans le domaine opératoire. 
Nous vous proposons de rejoindre des équipes de professionnels et professionnelles dans un environnement moderne et de pointe. Vous aurez la possibilité de participer à des interventions chirurgicales hautement spécialisées. Notre institution propose également des perspectives de développement des compétences et de développement de carrière. 
Nous vous offrons également la possibilité de participer à des projets de recherche clinique visant à faire évoluer les pratiques professionnelles et à apporter des améliorations continues.

Le poste concerne une activité en hémostase spécialisée, mais ce secteur fait partie du laboratoire d’Hématologie et d’Hémostase et dans ce cadre une activité en Hématologie est également possible en fonction des contraintes du laboratoire.
Dans le cadre de vos activités, vous réceptionnez les échantillons biologiques d'hémostase adultes et pédiatriques, et enregistrez les demandes d'examens selon les procédures en vigueur.
Vous utilisez les automates d’hémostase de routine et spécialisée Sysmex CN-6000 et CN-6500, GeneXpert Cepheid, BioFlash Ruwag, Chrono-Log et Apact 4004.
Vous validez techniquement et biologiquement les résultats d’hémostase de routine et spécialisée.
Vous participez aux cours et aux réunions du service.
Vous participez à l’assurance qualité au laboratoire : passage des CQI et des CQE, réalisation des tests pour les dossiers de vérification de méthode.
Vous effectuez des gardes et des piquets de weekend, de jours fériés et de nuits éventuellement en fonction des contraintes du laboratoire.

La population accompagnée présente majoritairement des situations de grande précarité. Les évaluations socio-financières sont fréquentes, tout comme les démarches en lien avec la régularisation, les prestations sociales ou la coordination avec les dispositifs d’aide du canton.
Dans ce contexte, l’écoute active, le soutien psychosocial, la capacité à établir un lien de confiance rapide, à identifier les enjeux et à élaborer des solutions concrètes et personnalisées sont des compétences clés.
Vous jouez un rôle essentiel pour garantir l’accès aux soins, la continuité des parcours et un accompagnement humain respectueux des réalités sociales et administratives des patients et patientes et de leurs proches.
Vous apportez votre expertise auprès des équipes médico-soignantes et assurez, en pluridisciplinarité, la liaison avec le réseau intra et extrahospitalier.

This is a graduate position within the QUEST programme, funded by the EOSC4ALL project of the European Commission. It is open to recent graduates in computer science, engineering or a related field. You do not need to tick every box or have every skill listed below, if you are motivated to learn, we encourage you to apply.
Join CERN's Storage and Data Management Group and help evolve the storage systems behind the Large Hadron Collider (LHC), while learning large-scale storage, cloud-native technologies and open-source software with the support of an experienced team.
You will work on CERNBox, the cloud storage used by the whole CERN community, from scientists to administrative staff. Your main task is to help make it interoperable with research infrastructures across Europe, through the Open Cloud Mesh (OCM) standard, and easy to deploy anywhere using Kubernetes. You will also explore how AI can help users find and use their data.
If you enjoy open standards, open source and building tools that many institutions can adopt, this is the place for you! You will be supported by experienced colleagues and learn from the whole team.
Your responsibilities
Develop and integrate backend and frontend software components.
Package and deploy interoperable services in distributed environments.
Support CERN community: you will join our operations team, troubleshooting incidents and supporting users.
Contribute your code, features and fixes back to the CERNBox open-source projects, working alongside a broader open-source community.
Work with partner institutions and research infrastructures across Europe to test, validate and refine these tools together.
Support users and partner teams as they adopt these tools, helping with troubleshooting and guidance.
Explore and prototype AI/ML capabilities for CERNBox, working with users to identify practical use cases. Prior AI/ML experience is welcome but not required.
Your profile
Experience with backend development in Go, and an interest in full-stack development.
Comfortable working in Linux environments and troubleshooting software and systems.
Familiarity with frontend development, ideally using JavaScript/TypeScript and Vue.js.
Software development experience from studies, projects, internships or open-source contributions, with a willingness to take ownership of features and to collaborate with others.
Ability to collaborate with users, technical teams and external partners.
Interest in open-source software, distributed systems and interoperability.
Skills
Backend: Go and API development.
Frontend: Modern frameworks such as Vue.js or similar technologies.
Systems: Linux, troubleshooting and software integration.
Cloud-native technologies: Containers, Docker, Kubernetes, Helm and CI/CD pipelines are an advantage.
Collaboration: Good communication skills and the ability to work effectively with technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Spoken and written English, with a commitment to learn French.
Eligibility criteria:
You are a national of a CERN Member or Associate Member State.
You have a professional background in Computing Engineer (or a related field) and have either:
a Master's degree with 2 to 6 years of post-graduation professional experience;
or a PhD with no more than 3 years of post-graduation professional experience.
You have never had a CERN fellow or graduate contract before.

Introduction
The CERN ATLAS Team plays a major role in the construction of the future silicon ATLAS Inner Tracker (ITk). In particular, the CERN Detector Technologies (DT) team focuses on the realisation of the Pixel Outer Barrel for the ITk. Our activities include the design, prototyping and assembly of the support structures and tooling as well as the final detector integration, installation and testing.

As a mechanical engineer in the CERN-DT Team, you will join the Engineering Office Section (EP-DT-EO) and work closely with personnel from the ATLAS Group (EP-ATL) and the Technical Coordination Team of the ATLAS Experiment on the design, construction and installation of the ATLAS ITk Pixel Outer System.
Functions
Design of precision tooling for the integration, testing and installation of the ITk Pixel Outer System Detector, comprising the Outer Barrel, Endcaps and Inner System Support Tube.
Design and develop service installation procedures and tooling, including temporary service management solutions for testing of the ITk Pixel Detector.
Verify the design of components and tooling according to the relevant standards and best engineering practices, performing both, analytical and numerical calculations.
Develop, document and implement tools and procedures for integration and installation of detector components and services.
Participate hands-on in the detector integration work in the ATLAS SR1 cleanroom as well as the preparation on surface and in the cavern for the installation.
Prepare technical specifications for components and tools, following up their production, acceptance and installation.
Support preparation of and participate in the ATLAS ID detector extraction.

Job Description Summary#LI-Hybrid
Location: Ljubljana, Slovenia / Barcelona, Spain

Vas navdušuje uporaba podatkovne znanosti in umetne inteligence za reševanje kompleksnih poslovnih izzivov in doseganje merljivega učinka?

Kot Podatkovni znanstvenik – svetnik (Associate Director, Data Science & Artificial Intelligence) boste sodelovali z različnimi poslovnimi področji, da bi razumeli kompleksne in ključne izzive ter jih pretvorili v celovite analitične pristope. Združevali boste učinkovito upravljanje podatkov, statistične metode, strojno učenje in umetno inteligenco z namenom pridobivanja uporabnih vpogledov, avtomatizacije ponovljivih procesov ter prispevanja k reševanju še neizpolnjenih medicinskih potreb.

Sodelovali boste pri upravljanju življenjskega cikla podatkov na ravni podjetja, od njihovega pridobivanja ali ustvarjanja, obogatitve in uporabe do hrambe in umika, ter zagotavljali razpoložljivost uporabnih, kakovostnih in točnih podatkov skozi njihov celoten življenjski cikel.

V sodelovanju z deležniki iz različnih delov organizacije boste kompleksne analitične ugotovitve pretvarjali v prepričljive poslovne vpoglede z učinkovito vizualizacijo, predstavitvami in podajanjem vsebin v ustreznem kontekstu. Samostojno boste sodelovali pri oblikovanju strategije, upravljanju proračunov, usklajevanju projektov ter zagotavljanju ustreznih virov na svojem področju odgovornosti.
-------------------------------
Are you passionate about using Data Science and Artificial Intelligence to solve complex business problems and make a measurable impact?

As Associate Director, Data Science & Artificial Intelligence, you will work across business domains to understand complex and critical challenges and translate them into integrated analytical approaches. You will combine effective data management, statistical methods, machine learning and Artificial Intelligence to generate actionable insights, automate repeatable processes and contribute to solving unmet medical needs.

You will help manage the lifecycle of enterprise data from acquisition or creation through enrichment, consumption, retention and retirement, supporting the availability of useful, clean and accurate data throughout its lifecycle.

Working with stakeholders across the organization, you will translate complex analytical findings into compelling business insights through effective visualization, presentations and contextual storytelling. You will independently help shape strategy, manage budgets, coordinate projects and ensure appropriate resourcing within your area of responsibility.

Where the role has people-management responsibility, you will empower, guide, coach and develop the team.

 
Job Description
Vaše ključne odgovornosti:
Preoblikovanje načina reševanja kompleksnih poslovnih izzivov z učinkovitim upravljanjem podatkov, podatkovno znanostjo, umetno inteligenco, statističnimi metodami in strojnim učenjem.
Pretvarjanje kompleksnih analitičnih ugotovitev v jasna priporočila za poslovne uporabnike ter uporaba učinkovite vizualizacije in pripovedovanja zgodb s podatki za vplivanje na strateške odločitve, tudi na ravni višjega poslovnega vodstva.
Vzpostavljanje učinkovitih pristopov k upravljanju podatkov za analitične namene ter prispevanje k razvoju zmogljivosti družbe Novartis na področju upravljanja podatkov in podatkovne znanosti.
Usklajevanje in določanje prioritet pri razporejanju virov med ključnimi pobudami ter proaktivno upravljanje spreminjajočih se zahtev, pričakovanj deležnikov, operativnih tveganj in konkurenčnih prioritet.
Sodelovanje z internimi deležniki, medfunkcijskimi ekipami, zunanjimi partnerji in institucijami pri reševanju ključnih poslovnih izzivov ter prepoznavanju priložnosti za izboljšanje operativne učinkovitosti in inovacije.
Ocenjevanje nastajajočih tehnologij, znanstvene programske opreme, orodij za vizualizacijo in računalniških pristopov ter izbira ustreznih orodij, podatkovnih virov in analitičnih tehnik za širok nabor poslovnih vprašanj.
Zagotavljanje agilnega svetovanja in raziskovalnih analiz za nujne in nestandardne poslovne izzive ter samostojno prepoznavanje relevantnih znanstvenih raziskav in uporaba ustreznih metodologij pri reševanju poslovnih izzivov.
Prispevanje k zunanji znanstveni skupnosti z znanstvenimi objavami, ki so bile predmet strokovnega recenzentskega postopka, sodelovanjem na strokovnih konferencah in v relevantnih medpanožnih delovnih skupinah.
Zagotavljanje poglobljenega znanstvenega in tehničnega strokovnega znanja. Opolnomočanje in razvoj zaposlenih, zagotavljanje mentorstva ter ustvarjanje okolja, ki podpira učinkovito izmenjavo znanja, razvoj in uspešnost.
Zagotavljanje skladnosti aktivnosti z veljavnimi zahtevami na področju kakovosti, etike, zdravja, varnosti in okolja ter veljavnimi odgovornostmi glede poročanja v zvezi z izdelki.

Zaželene izkušnje:
Izbira in izvajanje ustreznih strategij upravljanja podatkov in podatkovne znanosti za relevantne programe.
Doseganje ustreznih kontrolnih mejnikov programov upravljanja podatkov in napredne analitike ter pridobivanje potrebnih odobritev v okviru upravljavskih procesov.
Uspešno doseganje dogovorjenih ključnih kazalnikov uspešnosti (KPI) ter ciljev programov upravljanja podatkov in napredne analitike.

Nagrajevanje: 
V Novartisu smo zavezani k soustvarjanju prihodnosti medicine ter priznavanju in nagrajevanju ljudi, ki to omogočajo. 
 
Pričakovani letni osnovni razpon plače za delovno mesto:  
Slovenija: 67.130€ - 124.670€

Osnovna plača se določa na podlagi vnaprej opredeljenih in transparentnih kriterijev, kot so relevantne veščine, kompetence in izkušnje, ne glede na spol, ter v skladu z Novartisovo politiko določanja plač. Po zaposlitvi v Novartisu se plača periodično pregleda v skladu z internimi akti in postopki. 
 
Plačna enakost je temeljno načelo naše kadrovske politike in odraža našo zavezo k ustvarjanju raznolikega, pravičnega in vključujočega okolja, ki vse zaposlene obravnava dostojanstveno in spoštljivo, kot je opredeljeno v našem Kodeksu etike. 
 
Poleg osnovne letne bruto plače so zaposleni upravičeni tudi do spodaj navedenih ugodnosti: 
Letni bonus, ki pripada vsakemu zaposlenemu: 15% letne plače.
Regres za dopust: Leta 2025 je znašal 2.496 € (neto). Za leto 2026 znaša 2.678,28 € (neto). 
Nagrada za poslovno uspešnost: Leta 2025 je znašala 2.538,64 € (bruto), skupaj z zimskim regresom. 
Prostovoljno dodatno pokojninsko zavarovanje: Novartis v Sloveniji zagotavlja prostovoljno dodatno pokojninsko zavarovanje (5,844 % bruto izplačila, letno omejeno na 3.224,18 €). 
Zavarovanje: Dodatno nezgodno zavarovanje: V času zaposlitve pri Novartisu je zaposleni 24/7 zavarovan za primer smrti ali invalidnosti, ki bi bila posledica nezgode. Zavarovanje – Specialisti: Kolektivno zdravstveno zavarovanje, ki omogoča hitrejši dostop do specialističnih zdravstvenih storitev pri Zavarovalnici Triglav d.d. za vas in vaše družinske člane. 
Care Connect: Program, ki ponuja zaupno, osebno podporo za vaše duševno zdravje in dobro počutje s pomočjo terapij, svetovanj, orodij in še mnogo več. 
Ostale ugodnosti v skladu z zakonom in kolektivno pogodbo: Prevoz, prehrana ter ostali dodatki. 
 
Preberite brošuro in izvedite več o našem sistemu nagrajevanja: https://www.novartis.com/sites/novartis_com/files/novartis-life-handbook.pdf  
 
Opomba: Ugodnosti se lahko razlikujejo glede na državo ter so skladni z lokalno zakonodajo, vključno z določili kolektivnih pogodb. At Bristol Myers Squibb, our employees often ask, “Who are you working for?”—a question that fuels collaboration, accountability, and urgency in our work. Our purpose-driven culture inspires us to discover, develop, and deliver innovative medicines to prevail over serious diseases. We offer uniquely interesting and meaningful work, opportunities for growth, and a supportive environment that values inclusion, wellbeing, flexibility, and comprehensive benefits. This is work that transforms the lives of patients, and the careers of those who do it.

Shape the Future of Immunology & Cardiovascular Medicine

Are you a seasoned regulatory strategist ready to drive cutting-edge medicines through the European approval landscape? At BMS, we're looking for a bold, scientifically grounded Director, European Regulatory Strategy Lead to champion our Immunology & Cardiovascular (ICV) portfolio — from early development all the way through registration and lifecycle management.
This is your opportunity to sit at the heart of strategy, directly influencing how transformative therapies reach patients across Europe.

What You'll Do

As the European Regulatory Lead (ERL), you'll be the regulatory compass for your assigned Development Team(s), with the EU as your primary focus. In this role, you and the team will:
Define and drive EU regulatory strategy across development, registration, and lifecycle management
Lead negotiations with the EMA and other relevant Health Authorities, translating BMS strategy into real outcomes
Build integrated submission plans and translate them into operational deliverables for internal teams and external partners
Integrate scientific, medical, legal and business perspectives to achieve optimal regulatory outcomes
Provide authoritative regulatory guidance to Development Team Leaders and cross-functional stakeholders, proactively resolving complex issues
Monitor and anticipate evolving European and international regulatory trends, positioning BMS ahead of the curve
Build and nurture strong relationships with Health Authorities, alliance partners, and EU country colleagues

What You'll Bring

Education: A strong scientific/medical background — Ph.D., M.D., PharmD, MSc, or BSc in a relevant discipline.

Experience:
Extensive experience in regulatory affairs, with proven success delivering global/EU regulatory strategies
Prior experience in immunology and/or cardiovascular therapeutic areas (industry, health authority, or drug development) is preferred
A track record of successful Health Authority negotiations, including with the EMA
Experience leading cross-functional matrix teams in a complex, matrixed environment
Excellent written and verbal communication skills — you make the complex clear

Key Competencies:
Deep understanding of EU regulatory principles and procedures
Ability to integrate scientific, regulatory, and business thinking into practical, executable strategies
Resilient and decisive under pressure — you're comfortable navigating risk and driving resolution
A collaborative team player who works seamlessly across organisational, functional, and geographic boundaries

Travel required as appropriate.

Ready to lead regulatory strategy that matters? Apply now and bring your expertise to a team that's redefining what's possible in European regulatory science.

#LI-Hybrid

We hire for skills and capabilities, not just credentials – if this role excites you, but doesn’t perfectly match your resume, we encourage you to apply anyway.

How We Work
Where you work matters – because collaboration, innovation and patient impact happen in many settings. Our roles are structured across four work models: site-essential, site-by-design, field-based and remote-by-design. The model assigned to this role is based on its core responsibilities. Learn more at https://careers.bms.com/ways-of-working.

Visit careers.bms.com/eeo-accessibility to access our complete Equal Employment Opportunity statement.

Bristol Myers Squibb is Disability Confident – Employer

Director, Global Real-World Evidence & Health Outcomes Scientist, Oncology
 
For drugs to be successful, there must be robust health outcomes data to support launch optimization, reimbursement and maintain market positioning.  Specifically, evidence must be generated and maintained throughout the product lifecycle as the standard of care changes, new competitors are introduced, and patents expire on existing competitors. The landscape is evolving quickly as trials demonstrating efficacy in an area of unmet need may receive expedited review, or orphan product status designation which affects both GSK and competitors launch timelines and approval requirements. More of our customers are developing sophisticated internal health outcomes capabilities and access to real world data that can be used to better understand unmet needs and real-world effectiveness of our medicines. We need to better understand how our customers define value and to effectively collaborate with them to ensure we are generating value evidence data that includes real world evidence and cost effectiveness analyses that are impactful for payers, health systems, providers, and patients.
 
The role of Director, Global Real-World Evidence & Health Outcomes Research Scientist, Oncology is critical to achieving this ambition by supporting asset teams to ensure that each medicine GSK brings to market is supported by scientifically credible, high quality, evidence that drives competitiveness and strong evidence-based product positioning, value propositions and value-based pricing.  The role is critical to support the alignment of evidence with evidentiary requirements of customers responsible for marketing authorization, recommendation and reimbursement leading to successful patient access, product use and commercial success.
 
This role will provide YOU the opportunity to lead key activities to progress YOUR career.  These responsibilities include some of the following:
 
Plan, design and execute multiple studies for a given asset and manage timelines, deliverables, and budget.
Assure quality of deliverables, including review and sign off project specifications, protocols, data analysis plans, final study reports, abstracts, posters and manuscripts, in adherence to SOPs.
Identify resources, references and analyses to inform scientific design and advise internal experts (medical affairs, clinical, commercial/market access) and external experts as needed in support of the asset team.
Translate needs for evidence into study concepts in alignment with strategic objectives and vision for the asset, e.g. development of study protocols and proposing innovative and cost-effective ways of developing and executing studies.
Develop and maintain a good working knowledge of real-world data resources, existing partnerships and public initiatives and become the point person for select sources to advise on their suitability to address given research questions.
Develop a deep understanding of customers’ needs, including clinicians and HTA requirements, and their acceptance of different types of evidence and impact of that evidence to their decision making.
Collaborate with internal teams and participate in best practice sharing sessions across the non-interventional study organization.
Build strong working relationships with stakeholder groups across medical, market access, R&D and commercial to ensure strategic alignment and optimal cross-functional collaboration and communication. 
Ensure key stakeholders, including TA aligned business leaders, are regularly updated on plans through periodic reporting.
Develop excellent working relationships with external thought leaders to ensure appropriate methods and research agendas are applied, in accordance with GSK policies.

Basic Qualifications:

MSc, or equivalent in health outcomes, health economics, epidemiology, pharmacy, health or life sciences.
3+ years of experience working in the pharmaceutical industry, preferably in a multi-national company.
Experience in Oncology or Hematology
Experience in planning and delivering individual projects, managing budgets and working within a matrix setting.
A history of designing a variety of RWE (Real World Evidence) studies including prospective observational studies, cross-sectional and retrospective cohort studies, chart reviews, and database analyses.
Experience in utilizing evidence for the development of HTA submissions, reimbursement and/or medical engagements.
Experience delivering robust payer evidence and credibility to engage meaningfully with external experts and leaders in the field.
Experience with the diversity and complexity of healthcare markets, health technology assessment agencies, and reimbursement decision making globally, in region and local markets.
Experience in communicating technical and complex concepts and results to various audiences to impact decision-making.

Preferred Qualifications:
Advanced scientific degree, e.g. PhD, PharmD or equivalent in Health Economics, Outcomes Research, Epidemiology or similar.
Experience in prostate cancer.
Experience in Global and Country roles in oncology.
Launch experience.

Description
For candidates seeking to be located at our Stevenage site, this role will temporarily be based at Stevenage. However, the Company plans to relocate its offices to Cambridge, UK. The location of this role will therefore subsequently change to Cambridge, UK in accordance with timelines to be set by the Company. The relocation is currently proposed to take effect by early 2029.

At GSK, we have bold ambitions for patients, aiming to positively impact the health of 2.5 billion people by the end of the decade. Our R&D focuses on discovering and delivering vaccines and medicines, combining our understanding of the immune system with cutting-edge technology to transform people’s lives. GSK fosters a culture ambitious for patients, accountable for impact, and committed to doing the right thing, making sure that we focus our efforts on accelerating significant assets that meet patients’ needs and have the highest probability of success. We’re uniting science, technology, and talent to get ahead of disease together.
Find out more:
Our approach to R&D
 

Cancer is unrelenting, but so are we. At GSK, we are committed to transforming outcomes for people with cancer through innovative science, bold ambition, and strong partnerships across the healthcare ecosystem. We focus our science where it can matter most — advancing care in cancers with high unmet need, grounded in a deep understanding of disease biology and deliberate scientific choices that connect discovery to meaningful impact in the real world.

The Medical Director, Oncology Clinical Development - GU (Genitourinary) is the physician within the clinical program team, bringing medical expertise, clinical judgement, and a patient-centered perspective to the design, conduct, and interpretation of clinical studies. This role is accountable for medical monitoring and safety oversight, ensuring that patient safety and clinical integrity are maintained throughout study execution.

Operating within the clinical strategy defined by the Clinical Development Lead (CDL), the Medical Director partners closely with the Senior Scientist and cross-functional teams to ensure that the physician perspective is fully integrated into study delivery. The role serves as a core member of the Clinical Matrix Team (CMT), contributing to study-level decisions, investigator engagement, and regulatory interactions.

For more complex or multi-study programs, the Medical Director may provide medical guidance to other physicians within the program and contribute to broader clinical discussions that inform program-level decisions led by the CDL.

In This Role You Will:
Serve as the physician within the clinical program team, providing medical expertise across study design, conduct, safety oversight, and data interpretation
Lead medical monitoring activities for clinical studies, ensuring patient safety, clinical integrity, and compliance with the protocol and regulatory requirements
Interpret clinical and safety data from a physician perspective, generating insights that inform study-level and program-level decisions led by the CDL
Partner with the Senior Scientist and cross-functional teams to ensure medical considerations are integrated into study execution and delivery
Contribute medical expertise to protocol development, ensuring clinical relevance, patient safety, and feasibility within the framework defined by the CDL
Serve as a core member of the Clinical Matrix Team (CMT), providing the medical voice in study-level discussions and cross-functional decision-making
Engage with investigators and Key External Experts (KEEs) to support study conduct, scientific exchange, and external representation of the program
Contribute to regulatory documents, Health Authority interactions, and scientific communications from a physician perspective

Detailed Responsibilities:
Medical Monitoring and Safety Oversight
Lead medical monitoring activities for assigned clinical studies, including real-time clinical decision-making on patient eligibility, protocol-related medical queries, and safety oversight
Conduct and oversee medical review of clinical trial data, both directly and through oversight of delegated medical review activities
Interpret and contextualize safety data in collaboration with pharmacovigilance, ensuring appropriate signal detection, escalation, and benefit–risk assessment at the study level
Participate in safety review forums, including Safety Review Team (SRT) discussions, Independent Data Monitoring Committee (IDMC) data reviews, and internal governance as required
Ensure medical monitoring activities are conducted in compliance with GCP, ICH guidelines, and applicable regulatory frameworks

Study Design and Execution
Provide medical input into protocol development, ensuring clinical relevance, patient safety, and operational feasibility within the clinical strategy defined by the CDL
Apply clinical judgement to support protocol implementation, addressing medical questions that arise during study conduct and ensuring consistency with the study’s scientific objectives
Partner with the Senior Scientist to ensure that medical considerations are fully integrated into study execution, data generation, and operational delivery
Contribute to the development and review of key study documents, including the Informed Consent Form (ICF), protocol deviation management plan (PDMP), and study reference manual (SRM)
Provide medical input into clinical data generation activities, ensuring alignment with study objectives, patient safety considerations, and the Clinical Development Plan (CDP)

Data Interpretation and Scientific Contribution
Interpret clinical data from a physician perspective, translating findings into insights on safety, efficacy, and patient impact that inform decision-making by the CDL
Contribute to study-level and program-level data interpretation, supporting the CDL’s assessment of benefit–risk and clinical positioning
Contribute to the development of scientific communications, including study reports, clinical study summaries, publications, and congress materials
Collaborate with investigators on the evaluation and development of abstracts, posters, and manuscripts derived from clinical program data
Maintain current knowledge of the asset’s biological mechanism, disease landscape, evolving treatment paradigms, and competitive environment to inform clinical interpretation

Regulatory and External Engagement
Contribute medical expertise to regulatory documents and Health Authority interactions, including responses to clinical and safety queries
Support preparation of materials for regulatory submissions, advisory boards, and external engagements, providing the physician perspective on clinical data and safety
Engage with Key External Experts (KEEs), investigators, and scientific collaborators to support study conduct, scientific exchange, and relationship development
Represent the medical perspective at cross-departmental interactions, including Integrated Evidence Team (IET) and Medical Affairs strategy discussions, as delegated by the CDL
Contribute to the clinical and technical diligence assessment of business development opportunities as requested

Cross-Functional Collaboration and Clinical Matrix Team
Serve as a core member of the Clinical Matrix Team (CMT), providing medical leadership within study execution
Contribute medical expertise to disease area strategy, integrated evidence planning, and Medical Affairs discussions as appropriate
Collaborate across functions — including Clinical Operations, Biostatistics, Regulatory, and Pharmacovigilance — to ensure alignment on study objectives, patient safety, and data quality
Contribute to Oncology Clinical Development-wide initiatives and workstreams

Why You?

Working model
This role is hybrid. You will be on-site at one of the posted locations at least two days per week. Remote work is available on other days.

Basic Qualifications

Position Summary:

GSK is seeking to appoint a VP, Oncology Clinical Development Disease Area Head, reporting to the SVP, Head of Oncology Clinical Development. With accountability for the planning and implementation of the clinical development strategy across the Hematology portfolio, you will lead and contribute to strategic clinical positioning of early- and late-phase assets across their life-cycle with a cross-functional matrix team, at a pivotal moment for the organization as it sharpens its focus on pace, performance, portfolio delivery and bringing differentiated medicines to patients.

This role requires an experienced, cross-matrix senior leader capable of implementing and executing an integrated clinical strategy in support of the successful clinical development, translational research, regulatory filing and initial market launch of a growing portfolio of innovative and transformational Oncology therapies.

Clinical Development Strategy & Portfolio Leadership

Accountable for end-to-end clinical development of oncology assets from first-in-human (FTIH) studies through proof-of-concept studies, registrational trials, regulatory approval, and initial market launch, ensuring scientific rigor, speed, and quality of execution.

Shape and drive the scientific and clinical development strategy for assigned disease areas and assets, aligned with Oncology Tumor Team strategy and broader Oncology portfolio priorities.

Ensure deep integration of clinical, and disease-area expertise into preclinical and translational research activities to optimize asset positioning, biomarker strategy, and development strategy and decisions.

Evaluate, champion, and enable the use of novel approaches (e.g., AI/ML, innovative trial designs, external and real-world data sources) where they add clear scientific, operational, or decision-making value to clinical development.
Program Oversight, Governance & Visibility

Provide program-level oversight and leadership, while ensuring connectedness both cross functionally and across assets, maintaining visibility to progress, risks, dependencies, and trade-offs across the Oncology portfolio.

Serve as the senior clinical representative at key governance forums for assigned programs, ensuring strong clinical leadership, continuity, and high-quality decision-making.

Represent the Oncology Clinical Development organization internally and externally, including presenting at high-impact forums such as congress all-hands, senior leadership reviews, and advisory boards.

Lead scientific advisory boards and other external engagements to inform asset strategy, competitive positioning, and portfolio decisions, incorporating emerging science and external expert insight.
Cross-Functional Leadership & Connector Role

Co-lead asset development with matrix leadership partners, driving alignment across research, development, and commercialization planning, and ensuring cohesive execution against shared objectives.

Lead with an enterprise mindset: Act as a senior connector across functions, partnering closely with Oncology Research, Translational Research, Translational Medicine, Medical Affairs, Global Product Strategy, and

Build and sustain strong internal and external partnerships to accelerate decision-making, resolve complexity, and optimize development outcomes in a matrixed environment.

Line-manage and mentor Clinical Development Leads, Clinical Science Program Leads, Medical Directors, and Clinical Scientists, with clear accountability for performance, development, engagement, and succession planning.

Provide clarity on roles, expectations, and career paths within Oncology Clinical Development, contributing to role definitions, capability frameworks, and targeted training strategies.

Foster a culture of empowerment, enterprise-level drug development, scientific excellence, inclusion, and collaboration, aligned with OneOncology values, while modeling strong, visible leadership.

Actively remove organizational barriers and enable teams to operate effectively and autonomously within a complex, global matrix environment.
Standards, Processes & Continuous Improvement

Contribute to the establishment and continuous evolution of clinical development standards, processes, and best practices across Oncology, ensuring consistency, quality, and regulatory readiness.

Ensure timely access to relevant external scientific and competitive intelligence (e.g., congress data, emerging science, competitor activity) to inform clinical development decisions and portfolio strategy.

Regulatory Acumen: Familiarity with regulatory requirements and processes across major health authorities (FDA, EMA, etc.).

Innovation: Champion novel approaches to drug development, including biomarker-driven strategies, precision medicine, and immuno-oncology therapies.

Operating within the clinical strategy defined by the Clinical Development Lead (CDL), the Senior Medical Director partners closely with the Senior Scientist and cross-functional teams to guide the integration of physician expertise into study execution and programme-level decision-making. The Senior Medical Director provides matrixed oversight to the clinical team within the programme, supporting consistency of clinical judgement, safety evaluation, and medical interpretation across studies.

PLEASE NOTE: This career opportunity requires an on-site office presence (minimum of two days a week) at one of GSK’s Switzerland (Zug), UK (Stevenage or London HQ) or US (PA or MA) sites.

In This Role You Will:
Serve as a senior physician leader within the clinical programme, providing medical oversight and clinical insight across study design, conduct, and data interpretation
Provide guidance on medical monitoring and safety oversight across studies, ensuring consistent application of clinical judgement and patient safety standards
Interpret complex clinical and safety data, generating insights that inform programme-level decisions led by the CDL
Partner with the Senior Scientist and cross-functional teams to ensure medical considerations are integrated across study execution and programme delivery
Provide senior medical input into protocol development and study design, ensuring clinical relevance and patient-centred design within the clinical strategy defined by the CDL

consistency in approach, patient safety, and protocol adherence
Guide interpretation of safety data in collaboration with pharmacovigilance, supporting signal detection, escalation, and benefit–risk evaluation across the programme

Ensure medical monitoring approaches are aligned across studies and consistent with regulatory and organisational standards

Study Design and Execution
Provide senior medical input into protocol development across studies, ensuring clinical relevance, feasibility, and alignment with the clinical strategy defined by the CDL
Guide clinical aspects of study design and protocol implementation, particularly for complex, high-risk, or multi-study programmes
Support resolution of complex medical questions arising during study conduct, applying clinical judgement to inform programme-level decision-making
Ensure consistency of medical considerations across multiple studies within the programme

Data Interpretation and Scientific Contribution
Interpret complex clinical data across studies, integrating findings to inform programme-level insights on safety, efficacy, and patient impact
Contribute to programme-level data interpretation and support CDL-led benefit–risk assessment and clinical positioning
Guide development of scientific communications, including publications, congress materials, and clinical summaries
Maintain deep understanding of disease biology, evolving treatment paradigms, and competitive landscape to inform clinical interpretation and programme strategy

Regulatory and External Engagement
Contribute senior medical expertise to regulatory interactions and Health Authority discussions, including responses to complex clinical and safety queries
Represent the programme at advisory boards, steering committees, and external scientific forums, providing senior physician perspective on clinical data and programme direction
Engage with KEEs and scientific collaborators to support programme development, scientific exchange, and external credibility
Lead or contribute to the clinical and technical diligence assessment of business development opportunities

Cross-Functional Collaboration and Clinical Matrix Team
Serve as a senior member of the Clinical Matrix Team (CMT), influencing cross-functional alignment and programme-level decision-making
Contribute medical expertise to disease area strategy, integrated evidence planning, and Medical Affairs discussions
Collaborate across functions to ensure alignment on safety, data interpretation, and clinical positioning across the programme
Lead or contribute to Oncology Clinical Development-wide initiatives and workstreams

People Leadership & Capability Development
Provide oversight, guidance, and mentorship to clinical scientists within the programme, supporting consistency and quality of medical input across studies
Support development of clinical capability within the medical team, including coaching on medical monitoring, data interpretation, and external engagement
Contribute to talent development, performance discussions, and capability building within Oncology Clinical Development

Basic Qualifications:
Medical degree and completion of advanced specialty training, fellowship or country-equivalent higher-level qualification in medical oncology, pediatric oncology or hematology.
Experience in sarcoma oncology, including leading drug development.
Clinical and pharmaceutical experience in oncology clinical development, with depth across multiple studies or programmes
Experience in medical monitoring, safety evaluation, and clinical data interpretation across clinical studies
Understanding of clinical development processes, GCP, ICH guidelines, and global regulatory frameworks
Experience operating within cross-functional matrix teams and contributing to complex clinical and programme-level decisions

Preferred Qualifications:
Deep expertise in soft tissue sarcoma and osteosarcoma, including experience leading or supporting clinical development programs across early and/or late-stage clinical studies.
Strong scientific communication and stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to influence internal and external audiences
Deep experience in oncology clinical development across multiple studies or programmes, including Phase I–III
Experience contributing to or leading aspects of regulatory interactions (e.g., IND, scientific advice, NDA/MAA)
Demonstrated experience engaging with KEEs, advisory boards, and scientific communities in oncology
Track record of scientific publications and congress presentations
